items.label: No. 132
items.sum: The new President thanks members for electing him and calls for united effort to make the club's seventieth year its most outstanding.
items.s: THE PRESIDENTS MESSAGE The new President thanks members for electing him and calls for united effort to make the club's seventieth year its most outstanding. Fellow Members, I have already had an opportunity of conveying to those members who were present at the Annual General Meeting my sincere thanks for electing me as your President for the ensuing year and now it is possible, through the medium of the Belgravian, to tell you all how delighted I am to receive the highest honour the Club can bestow on one of its members. It is my earnest hope that during this, our seventieth year, we shall not only repeat some of our major successes of former years but add new achievements to our already very fine record of which I am sure we have every right to be proud. This can only be realised by the concerted efforts of every member of the Club, Seniors, Juniors and Youths alike. You have selected the officers for the management of our various branches of athletics, and only by giving them your undivided support, both in training and in competition, can we hope to achieve our goal. There is no doubt that we have an abundance of talent which, combined with determination, energy, enthusiasm and loyalty to the Club will, I am sure, make this seventieth year of Belgrave the most outstanding in the history of the Club and leave me with many happy recollections of my year as President. Yours sincerely Sydney Roberts. Sydney Roberts Sydney Roberts President

items.h: BELGRAVE 20 MILES OPEN ROAD RACE AND CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP
items.sum: Report of the Belgrave 20 miles open road race and club championship held in heat of about 90 degrees, with Alan Bishop becoming club 20 mile champion.
items.s: BELGRAVE 20 MILES OPEN ROAD RACE AND CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP Report of the Belgrave 20 miles open road race and club championship held in heat of about 90 degrees, with Alan Bishop becoming club 20 mile champion. Held on the 6th July, this event once again proved a very severe test, as the temperature on this occasion was in the region of 90 degrees. So regularly does this occur, that anyone desiring a nice(?) hot day on the beach need only to arrange for it to coincide with the date of our Open "20". Seventy-six runners were started on their way by Arthur Whitehead's "Atomic Device" and soon afterwards Jones of Southend was seen to be leading from Eric Gebbett. Unfortunately Eric is allergic to the sun and after about two miles he began to drop back and on Copse Hill he was overtaken by Alan Bishop, who then led in the Club Championship. The retirement of Arthur Penstone after two laps meant that we were out of the team race, but Eric ran on pluckily, although obviously not enjoying the conditions. He was, however, unable to catch Alan who finished 12th after a very shrewd run, to become our new 20 mile champion. A very courageous performance came from Conway, who was determined to finish at all costs and did so to gain 3rd place in the championship. The winner of the Open race was never in doubt, for Jones, now 41 years of age, defied the heat to win by a wide margin in the very good time of 1hr.56m.7s. Second was Ken Honney of Walton in 2h.0[illegible]m.44s. and third, P. Vivian of T.V.H. in 2h.01m.39s. The team result resulted in a win for Walton with T.V.H. second and Finchley H. third. The organisation of the race was, as usual, flawless and Bill Bird and Arthur Whitehead must be congratulated on a very fine piece of work. Nor should the unstinting efforts of the many helpers be overlooked, for without their assistance the race could not possibly have been a success. Result of the Club Championship:- Also started:- A. items.sum: Report of the 'B' team match against Lensbury and H.H.H. at Sydenham on 5th June, with Charlie Jones winning both sprints.
items.s: 'B' Match v. Lensbury and H.H.H. Report of the 'B' team match against Lensbury and H.H.H. at Sydenham on 5th June, with Charlie Jones winning both sprints. Sydenham 5th June. For this meeting, which was termed a 'B' team fixture, Belgrave turned out six worthy representatives. Charlie Jones, as expected, gained a victory in both the sprints and was also placed 3rd in the Long Jump. Gerry Leroy ran very well in the half-mile to take 3rd place - he must have done his best ever. The race was won by Linford (T.V.H.) for Lensbury in 2m.0.8s., on a five laps to the mile grass track. Dudley Gordon was unlucky not to win the 440, losing by inches, after leading all the way - he also doubled up in the 100yds. D. Edmunds and B. Trower finished 4th and 5th in the mile to give us extra points. The latter also took 3rd place in the 3 miles and took part in the Javelin. In the relay our team of Gordon, Fox, Jones and Leroy only missed the ground record by one fifth of a second. As our President said afterwards when giving our thanks for a first class supper, "we were few in number but ability and keenness were there". It is a great pity there was not more support for this meeting as the evening was so perfect. The only other thing that was missing, according to Charlie Jones, was "talent"! Brian C. Trower. Detailed results are not yet to hand. Charlie Jones Charlie Jones won both sprints, 3rd long jump Gerry Leroy Gerry Leroy 3rd half-mile Linford Linford won half-mile for Lensbury in 2m.0.8s. items.sum: Walking notes: a Belgrave-led team win in a 52 kilometre race in Belgium, Stan Vickers' A.A.A. 2 miles title, the Outer Circle 25 miles team win in Birmingham and other walking performances.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS Walking notes: a Belgrave-led team win in a 52 kilometre race in Belgium, Stan Vickers' A.A.A. 2 miles title, the Outer Circle 25 miles team win in Birmingham and other walking performances. As a result of our contribution to the Union of London Walking Clubs a team of four travelled to Chalaroi in Belgium for a 52 kilos. event. The team consisted of D. Thompson (Met.W.C.) and three Belgrave lads - G. Checkley, G. Beecham and H. McGreechan. They were met by Harry Shields who went over for a few days holiday and his assistance proved very useful on the day of the race. The race which took place on Sunday 7th July resulted in a clear win for our team with Thompson the winner in a course record of 4h.30m.10s., Checkley second in 4h.52m.40s., Beecham third in 4h.57m.54s. and McGreechan fifth in 5h.08m.57s. A novel feature of this race was that, owing to the water supply being turned on for only two hours per day our men had to use Vichy Water for spongeing and drinking purposes. However, it didn't have any ill effects as the result showed. The team returned on the Monday, leaving Harry the Man of Kent in 'Ghent' to wander home in his own time. E.A.Smith put up his best performance of the season when finishing second in the London Business Houses 2 miles Championship at Hurlingham in the good time of 14m.28.4s. R.Switzer continued to shew improvement by clocking 15.54 to finish sixth. J.G.Coleman and R.Middleton were 1st and 2nd respectively in the 2 miles handicap at the Vickers Armstrong meeting at Weybridge on the 29th of June. Congratulations to Stan Vickers on his fine victory in the A.A.A. 2 miles Championship - his first A.A.A. title. Stan's time was 14m.5.6s. and in addition he won the style prize. Other Club finishers were Ted Smith(4th in 14.36.2) and Eric Hall(6th in 14.40.4). On the same day (July 13th) we sent a team to Birmingham to defend our team title in the Outer Circle 25 miles Walk,which we duly accomplished in no uncertain manner by scoring 16 pts. to Leicester W.C's 36 and Royal Sutton Coldfield's 51. Hugh McGreechan was 4th in 3h.49m.38s., Bob Newson 5th in 3.52.27, George Checkley 11th in 4.0.42, Bernard Eglinten 12th in 4.3.21, Fred Rolfe 15th in 4.7.35 and Harry Shields 16th in 4.8.12. After the race a news reporter said to Harry, "we have a competitor here who is aged 55, are you older than that?" Harry's reply can best be imagined ! So ended a perfect day. D. Thompson D. items.sum: Report of the club meeting at Battersea Park on 22nd July where the hop step and jump and 3 miles club championships were decided, won by N. Caves and P. Newell.
items.s: CLUB MEETING AT BATTERSEA PARK 22nd JULY Report of the club meeting at Battersea Park on 22nd July where the hop step and jump and 3 miles club championships were decided, won by N. Caves and P. Newell. Two Club Championships were decided at this meeting and the entries for both were very encouraging. In the Hop Step & Jump, a keen battle ensued between Norman Caves, Charlie Jones and Ivan Mayers. Norman eventually won with a 44'9" effort, but one wonders just how far Ivan would have got had he not repeatedly taken off well before the board - a very interesting contest to watch. 1st N.Caves 44'9". 2nd C.Jones 43'10½". 3rd I.Mayers 43'8" The 3 miles, with a field of 25, proved that we could really start putting teams in 2 mile races, for some excellent times were recorded. Davies, Newell and Hallowell led the field after an early dash by Frank Wright. For some unaccountable reason Davies almost stopped with three laps to go and so the race became a duel between Newell and Hallowell. The latter, however, could not hold Newell when he made his effort ½ mile out to become a clear winner in 14m.21.8s. which was a new Championship best performance. Without wishing to criticize Newell, it did seem that had he possessed the confidence to leave Hallowell at the two mile point, he would have got near to 14 minutes. D.McLean ran through well to secure third place while Davies made a good recovery to finish fourth. 1 P.Newell 14.21.8; 2,B.Hallowell 14.30.4; 3, D.McLean 14.50.8 4, T.Davies 15.1; 5, R.Linstead 15.2; 6, J.Masters 15.3. items.h: CORONATION TROPHY MEETING AT CARSHALTON. JULY 20th.
items.sum: Report of the Coronation Trophy meeting at Carshalton on 20th July, where four Belgrave members won the Trophy by two points.
items.s: CORONATION TROPHY MEETING AT CARSHALTON. JULY 20th. Report of the Coronation Trophy meeting at Carshalton on 20th July, where four Belgrave members won the Trophy by two points. Only four members turned up for this meeting, but it proved to be enough. In the 100 yds. Charlie Jones won his heat in 10.5s. and Dennis Butler was third in his, so both our men were in the final. After this Dennis went over to throw the javelin and Charlie proceeded to make his presence felt in the long jump. Dennis eventually finished third with about 113 ft. (not a personal best), and Charlie finished up by winning with a jump of 20'11". In between jumps and throws Dennis and Charlie both won their heats in the 220 yds (this sounds rather hectic). Gerry Leroy was bullied into running the 880 yds. and finished very fast to be placed second in 2m.0.6s. In the final of the 100 yds., Charlie, for some unknown reason was left at the start, but Dennis didn't wait for him and finished fifth in about 10.6. After this, Charlie returned to his high and long jumping and managed 5'4" in the high to be placed third. Meanwhile, Tubby Jones was winning the shot with a fairly good putt, and Gerry Leroy was walking his speciality - the 440 yds.- in 51.3s., a good time in the gusty conditions. In the 220 yds., Charlie was a good winner in 24.0s. and Dennis was just pushed out of second place. We won the Trophy by two points. "Oats and Barley" Charlie Jones Charlie Jones won 100 yds heat in 10.5s. Dennis Butler Dennis Butler 3rd in 100 yds heat; javelin Gerry Leroy Gerry Leroy 2nd 880 yds in 2m.0.6s.; 440 yds in 51.3s. Tubby Jones Tubby Jones won the shot Coronation Trophy Meeting Carshalton

items.sum: Belgrave walkers took 1st, 2nd, 8th, 9th and 15th places in the A.A.A. 7 miles track walk at Watford, won by Stan Vickers, who also took the style prize.
items.s: A.A.A. 7 MILES TRACK WALKING CHAMPIONSHIP Belgrave walkers took 1st, 2nd, 8th, 9th and 15th places in the A.A.A. 7 miles track walk at Watford, won by Stan Vickers, who also took the style prize. This event was held on the 10th of August at Watford and it resulted in an excellent display of Belgrave track-walking strength, with Club vests occupying 1st, 2nd, 8th, 9th and 15th places. Stan Vickers, as expected, was first home in 51m.34.3s. and he was also awarded the style prize, so completing a "double double" as he also carried off both individual and style awards in the 2 miles walk earlier in the season. He was closely followed by Eric Hall who was only 15 sec. behind - an excellent performance. The biggest surprise of the day came from Nic Milsum, who in his first senior 7 mile track race, finished 8th in 55m.6s. This was 54 sec. inside A.A.A. standard, and of course qualifies him for a Senior Club Honours Badge. Ted Smith was only 7 sec. behind in 9th place and he too gains an Honours Badge. Ray Hall was unlucky to miss standard by only 19 sec. but we feel certain he will achieve it next year. What a pity there is no team race in this event ! Stan Vickers Stan Vickers 1st in 51m.34.3s. and style prize Eric Hall Eric Hall 2nd, 15 sec. behind Nic Milsum Nic Milsum 8th in 55m.6s., first senior 7 mile track race; Senior Club Honours Badge Ted Smith Ted Smith 9th, 7 sec. behind Milsum; Honours Badge Ray Hall Ray Hall missed standard by 19 sec. A new Club record was put up for this distance by Len Bishop when he finished 11th in 2hrs.30 m.47s. Other Club members taking part were, Eric Gebbett 23rd in 2H.42m.56s., Alan Bishop 29th in 2h.51m.7s. and Eric Bishop 36th in 3h.1m.57s. items.s: HASTINGS TO BRIGHTON OPEN WALK. AUG.17TH Belgrave won the team race in the Hastings to Brighton open walk on 17th August with three of the first four, despite George Checkley going off course. We had eight representatives in this event and by finishing three in the first four, comfortably won the team race from Surrey Walking Club. Early in the race George Checkley and Thompson of Met. items.s: CLUB 6 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP (TOM CARTER CUP) AUG.21ST. Second-claim member Bill Bird won the club 6 miles race in 29m.37s., with Pete Newell retaining the club title (Tom Carter Cup) in 29m.55s. A good field turned out for this race, including Bill Bird our second claim member, and of course Pete Newell the holder. From the start Bill took the field along at a very brisk pace and by the half distance only Pete Newell was still with him. Over the last two miles Bill gradually pulled away to win in the excellent time of 29m.37s. He is of course ineligible for the Club Championship and so the title was retained by Pete who finished second in 29m.55s., the best winning time so far. Another member to run well was George Flanagan who was almost a minute ahead of the third man, D. McLean. Result:- 1. P. Newell 29.55; 2. G. Flanagan 30.30; 3. D. McLean 31.29; 4. P. items.s: BOYS & YOUTHS COMPETITION Report and points table of the boys' and youths' multi-event competition, won by C.A. Page (boys) and Trevor Hart (youths), with Malcolm Draper in hospital. The contest in the boys' section resolved itself into a duel between C.A.Page, 14½ yrs., and Derek Wade, 13½ yrs; the former winning by one point. R.Ponton was third. Although 14 boys took part in the competition, only the first two competed in four or more events. Any of the next six point scorers could have been third in the competition merely by completing four events. It would appear that here is scope for a little more persistance. In the youths' section, Malcolm Draper was all set to secure a maximum of 24 points, having already won the high and long jumps, and being the holder of the 'Chandler' Cup, should have won the 100 yds; there being no doubt about scoring top points in the javelin. Unfortunately Malcolm was taken ill, and is at present in hospital. We all wish him a speedy recovery. However, he was second, with only three events, to the very persistent efforts of Trevor Hart, who was the only youth to compete in all six events, and who well deserved his win. RESULT Name. 880YDS. items.sum: New Year editorial urging members to make resolutions to support fixtures, help run the club, care for Belgrave Hall and encourage and train young members.
items.s: New Year editorial urging members to make resolutions to support fixtures, help run the club, care for Belgrave Hall and encourage and train young members. To all fellow Belgravians, at home and overseas, we send our wishes for a HAPPY AND SUCCESSFUL NEW YEAR. We would like to continue in a festive, happy vein, but the general apathy in the Club during 1957 has got to be remedied and we would respectfully like to offer some suggestions. Let your new year's resolutions be :- To turn out in every possible match be it home or away, A or B fixture. A mob match should be supported as such and you cannot call a turn-out of less than 100 a "mob". To take a greater interest in Club affairs; our present officers, even if willing, cannot go on for ever. Young blood, young thought and young ideas are needed. To see that greater care is taken of Club property, Belgrave Hall is the envy of many clubs, but without proper attention it would soon become a heavy liability. Your subs are low - help to keep them so. To give the necessary encouragement to all those young members on whose shoulders our future rests. A friendly word of advice or encouragement from a V.I.P. can have a tremendous effect. To assist in the training of our youngsters; this applies to those whose racing days are over. The Club has given you much, plough some of your experience back. Above all, remember that we all want Belgrave Harriers to become the leading name in athletics in all its spheres. Let this be our aim for 1958. Belgrave Hall

items.s: By the way Club notes on members' marriages, Colin Collis's form, Len Adams's comeback, Civil Service cross-country placings and Bob Plummer's recovery. Congratulations to Syd James and George Beecham on their recent marriages. Colin Collis is weakening; having bashed the Club '7' and run quite well he only needs a few well directed words and perhaps he'll be changing in the stable at Windsor Castle again in 1958. Len Adams is making a welcome comeback. An unassuming chap, he will be a valuable asset to our long distance road running department Chas Walker was placed third in the Civil Service 5 miles cross-country championship and Dave Baulch was eighth. Bob Plummer, now recovered from his knee trouble plans a full season for 1958. items.sum: Report of the club's Annual General Meeting of 20 September, covering the officers' reports, finances, Syd Roberts's election as President and life-membership for Eric Hall and Stan Vickers.
items.s: ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING Report of the club's Annual General Meeting of 20 September, covering the officers' reports, finances, Syd Roberts's election as President and life-membership for Eric Hall and Stan Vickers. Held on the 20th September this meeting attracted barely one tenth of the total Club membership. This is the only occasion during the year when members can give their assistance in deciding the management of the Club by taking part in the election of officers, but having left this difficult task to the few who were present, it is hoped that they will show their approval by giving full support to those who were elected. The Hon. Secretary's report, a copy of which you received, was adopted with a few minor amendments. This was followed by the Hon. Treasurer's report which revealed a small profit on the General Account, but he pointed out that with the increase in the cost of postage from 1st October and the general trend of rising prices, there was every need to keep a close watch on expenditure if this state of affairs was to be maintained. The amount outstanding last year in connection with the improvements to the Club premises has now been paid, and allowing for depreciation there was a small loss on the year's working. He next informed the meeting that the cost of maintaining the various services at the hall, including rates etc., was now £350 per annum, and in order to make provision for re-decorating and further improvements in the future it was essential to concentrate on building up a good reserve. Tribute was then paid to the work of Les Cohen in connection with the Supporters Club and to those who had given him valuable assistance during the past year. The accounts were then adopted and a hearty vote of congratulations was accorded to the Hon. Treasurer. In order to facilitate the smooth progress of the meeting the election of officers was then dealt with. The retiring President, Tom Carter, on behalf of the Committee, informed the meeting that their unanimous recommendation for the office of President was Syd Roberts and formally proposed him, giving a brief account of his 21 years as a member. This was supported by Harry Shields and on being put to the meeting was unanimously carried. The newly elected President then took the chair and thanked all members for the honour just received. The election of officers then proceeded in normal rotation, details of which will be found in the new handbook. The Chairman paid tribute to the work of Alf Harley, the General Hon. Secretary, and thanked him for continuing in the office. Whilst the counting of votes for the ten members of the new Committee was being dealt with, Jack Goswell rose on behalf of the outgoing Committee and put forward its recommendation, in accordance with Club Rules, that Eric Hall and Stan Vickers be elected to life-membership, giving a detailed account of their progress in race walking which had culminated in their selection to represent Great Britain in the Olympic Games at Melbourne. After being seconded, there was some discussion on the merits of other members of the Club, following which a vote was taken and the resolution passed by a sufficient majority. After the new committee had been announced the only item left on the agenda was "Other business, if any". The Chairman then proposed a hearty vote of thanks to the retiring President for his work during the past year. This was carried unanimously and the meeting closed with a vote of thanks to the Chairman. items.s: LONDON TO BRIGHTON WALK SEPT. 14TH. Report and result of the London to Brighton walk, which incorporated the club championship for the Belgrave Cup, with Belgrave's A team winning the team race on a record low score. A new record low score in the team race was achieved by the Club when the team finished their four scorers in 1st,3rd,4th and 5th positions for a total of 13 pts., individual positions, of course, being deleted. The fact that the race incorporated the Club Championship for the "Belgrave Cup" no doubt contributed to this remarkable feat, for nothing will spur a Belgrave Harrier on more than the sight of another Club man in front. Indeed, such was the fierceness of the contest that Harry Shields who was 10th in the open race could only get 5th in the Club Championship. We also finished a "B" team, in 4th place - well ahead of many "A" teams . Thanks are due to the many willing helpers, attendants and supporters who helped to make this such a memorable day. items.label: No. 133
items.h: LONDON TO BRIGHTON RELAY (SOUTHERN CLUBS) OCT.12TH.
items.sum: Stage-by-stage report by "Olympian" of Belgrave's recovery from 18th after the first leg to second place in the London to Brighton relay for southern clubs, won by Thames Valley Harriers.
items.s: LONDON TO BRIGHTON RELAY (SOUTHERN CLUBS) OCT.12TH. Stage-by-stage report by "Olympian" of Belgrave's recovery from 18th after the first leg to second place in the London to Brighton relay for southern clubs, won by Thames Valley Harriers. Once again we were blessed with the best of weather and no matter what the result our supporters were all set for a good day out. For those who have never followed this race I can fully commend it as the best and most enjoyable in the athletic calendar, both from the competitors and spectators points of view. The changing fortunes of the teams provide a great spirit of friendly rivalry and the quality of the racing gives a piquant spice to a day of many thrills. Those in the know forecast a Thames Valley victory and for once their prognostications proved correct. It would have taken an "Old Moore" to have placed the other teams in the right order. Belgrave were generally considered as being a club with a chance of making the first six with Polytechnic, Woodford Green, Herne Hill, Essex Beagles and St.Albans as the main rivals. Little did we realise the early misfortune that was to befall us and the valiant fight that the rest of the team was to make to recover our prestige. Don MacLean had been given the first leg to Wandsworth Common and the first stroke of ten o'clock sent him on his way with nineteen other runners. At first, all was well, but by the time Chelsea Bridge was reached it was obvious that it was not Don's day and as we have seen so often in the past he fell back and back and our early hopes fell and fell until by the end of the stage we were in eighteenth place and over 1½ mins. behind the leading club (Aylesford P.M.). This was disaster, and a gap which would need a lot of closing. Charlie Walker, however, was spurred on by the responsibility thrown on his shoulders and set out to recover some of the lost ground. By excellent running he passed team after team and the encouraging cheers of the few supporters on this leg kept him at his task. At Mitcham we were up to 9th place but still 1½ mins. behind Poly. who had taken over the lead through a great run by John Evans. Charlie was the second fastest of the day. George Flanagan, one of our youngest team members, had the difficult leg from Mitcham to Purley. His steady start was a wise move, and with the help of Llewellyn of Walton, who caught him after a mile, he made good progress on the field ahead, and by Purley had reduced the overall lead to 69 sec. and had gained a further place - an invaluable effort. Charlie Dabbs took the fourth stage but was obviously not at his best and we were disappointed to see our much improved position slipping away again. Charlie fought hard to keep his place but at Merstham we were back again to 9th and 2¼ min. behind Thames Valley who had gone into what proved to be a winning lead. Jim Masters on the switchback course through Redhill and Earlswood again gave us hope by passing three clubs and taking us up to 6th. Thames Valley, however, were represented by Norris and added 10 more seconds to their lead. Jim produced the second best time and closed up the gap on the intervening clubs - an excellent effort. The next leg was a new one of little more than two miles in length and John Davies, complete with an arm in plaster following a fracture, was entrusted with it. This was John's first experience of this type of racing and he later suffered from an over zealous start which diminished his finishing power. He was forced back to 8th by Portsmouth and Shaftsbury and at this point we were 2¾ min. behind Thames Valley, who were 500 yds. ahead of the second club, Woodford. This run should prove very valuable to John and we shall expect some first class performances from him in future races. Peter Hitchcock had the joy of running over the newly laid stretch of road round Gatwick Airport and although losing ground on the leading clubs he managed to pull us back to 7th with a steady performance which should add to his experience for next year. We were now well over half way to Brighton and no less than 3 min. 10 sec. behind - a poor prospect and we were wondering whether even a place in the first six was to be gained. Pat Newell, taking over Jack Brown's cloak, proved a worthy successor on the hard grind from Crawley to Handcross, and in gaining two places brought us within sight of all but T.V.H. who had widened their lead,through a grand run by Bert Ingles, to 2½ minutes over the second club, Woodford. Pat, despite an unplanned trip under the subway at Crawley level-crossing, which loses at least ten seconds, was credited with the third best time of the day. Eric Gebbett's turn came next on the long undulating leg from Handcross to "The Castle" at Hickstead. This leg is generally reserved for the best runners of each club, and our difficulty, in recent years, has been to find someone of sufficient calibre to keep on equal terms with other teams. Eric gave of his best and ran a good race, but unfortunately he lost a considerable amount of ground on the leaders, and our sixth position, with only three legs to go, was far from favourable with T.V.H. over five minutes ahead and other clubs well away. Len Bishop, on the tenth stage, thought we still had a chance, and with a run which gave him the fastest time of the day, picked up one place which brought us up to fifth, only 12 seconds behind the third and fourth teams. T.V.H., by this time, were in an invincible position with over three minutes to spare on Woodford, who were still holding on to second place. Dave Baulch, again selected to run up Dale Hill, joined in the spirit of the chase and soon moved up to third place and was gaining fast on Woodford, who had by this time run all their best men and were beginning to flag badly. Dave ran to such purpose that he achieved the best time of the day and brought us to within nine seconds of Woodford - a magnificent performance. Our supporters were wild with excitement and were giving our runners every encouragement possible - never have stop-watches worked so hard in taking time checks. Brian Hallowell set about the last leg in a very workmanlike manner, much to the consternation of the Woodford runner only a short distance ahead - never have I seen anyone look so worried. Across Preston Park in similar manner as in April last, Brian took over second place and went clean away from the Woodford man and reached the Aquarium 36 seconds ahead. He also had the distinction of recording the fastest time of the day. It is doubtful if any team, after such a bad start, has ever recovered in so grand a manner to take one of the major awards and keep the Belgrave flag flying so high. Our record in these races is second to none, and the prospects of even greater improvement are considerable, with a batch of first class material available for selection next April coupled with the solid and experienced strength of our seasoned performers. items.sum: Report and result of the Smiths of England 12½ mile road race at Witney, won as a team by Belgrave, with Eric Gebbett third.
items.s: SMITHS OF ENGLAND 12½ MILE ROAD RACE. NOV.2ND AT WITNEY Report and result of the Smiths of England 12½ mile road race at Witney, won as a team by Belgrave, with Eric Gebbett third. Thanks to the efforts of Jack Goswell, a pleasant trip by coach was organised to transport the walkers to Oxford, for their match against the University, and the runners to Witney for the above mentioned race. Our story concerns the latter event, where we were welcomed by Derek Burfitt and Verne Blowfield, two well known ex-members. They had prepared the race with great attention to detail; the result could not be faulted. Excellent showers, good road surfaces, FREE EATS and first rate prizes ensured that our hungry brigade will make every effort to compete next year. For the record book, Eric Gebbett excelled over the distance and the extra two miles enabled him to move away from Chas. Walker and finish third to Haslam of T.V.H. and Thornton of Leeds. Chas. ran well to finish fifth with Len Bishop pipping his brother Eric for third scoring place. items.sum: Report and Belgrave results from the South of the Thames junior cross-country at Reigate Priory, where George Flanagan was second.
items.s: SOUTH OF THE THAMES "JUNIOR" REIGATE PRIORY. NOV.9TH Report and Belgrave results from the South of the Thames junior cross-country at Reigate Priory, where George Flanagan was second. We fielded four teams with a total of twenty-seven runners over a well laid out and sporting course in good conditions. George Flanagan was soon prominent and ran an extremely good race throughout to come through from fifth at the halfway stage to second, only eleven seconds behind the winner Bill Bird of Ranelagh who is a second claim Belgrave member. Our other runners were too far back to secure a place in the team race and they finished 7 th with 130 pts. Robin Weate, in his first big race for us, shewed that he will be a very useful asset by finishing 28th. Charlie Dabbs was disappointing in 44th position but has been unfit and was short of training. Don Stroud ran well to finish 56th and others who performed satisfactorily were S.Boreham,C.Shippen, J.Dooley and M.Robinson. Don McLean came all the way from Oxford by motor-cycle to finish 324th - perhaps the cold got into his bones, or is there some other reason for these continuous lapses from his real form? items.h: MATCH v. HERNE HILL AT ADDINGTON NOV.16TH
items.sum: Report of the cross-country match against Herne Hill at Addington, lost in senior and junior races but won by the youths.
items.s: MATCH v. HERNE HILL AT ADDINGTON NOV.16TH Report of the cross-country match against Herne Hill at Addington, lost in senior and junior races but won by the youths. Probably due to our Club Dinner being on the same evening we could muster only eleven seniors, four juniors and five youths for this fixture but a good run was had by all. In the senior event we were short of our best performers but it was good to see Archie Bedford once more in our midst and even more refreshing to see him running well enough to be our first man home in fourth place. The juniors ran in the same race and Charlie Dabbs and Robin Weate followed Archie round, closely pursued by Eddie Short and Clive Shippen. The brothers Bishop (Alan and Eric) indulged in some good pack running with Jim Heathfield and Bob Glover in attendance. The final reckoning gave Herne Hill a win by 95 pts. to 115 in the senior and 18 to 20 in the junior. In the youths race which had been run earlier young Thresher showed delightful form to win by 15 sec. with Trevor Hart in third place. This good start enabled us to win the team race by the narrow margin of one point - 27 to 28. Vickers second and E. Hall third. The 38th annual Open Walk, which is the oldest and, we feel, the most popular 7 in the calendar, took place in perfect weather and attracted a record field of 230 starters. With Eric Hall in such fine form and Stan Vickers out for the first time since August and the rest of our team walking well, we were very hopeful of retaining our team title. Right from the start Eric and Stan, in company with K.Matthews of Royal Sutton Coldfield, took the field along at a record-breaking pace, with the result that the first five finishers beat the old course record. Our thanks are due to the Prize Fund Donors without whose generosity we could not maintain our fine display of prizes, also to Arthur Whitehead who, by placing his premises at our disposal, did much to relieve congestion at the hall. items.h: MATCH v. FINCHLEY H., BRIGHTON A.C. AND St.ALBANS CITY A.C.NOV.30TH. at Ruislip
items.sum: Report and Belgrave results of the four-club cross-country match at Ruislip, won by Belgrave with Charlie Walker second to Hugh Foord.
items.s: MATCH v. FINCHLEY H., BRIGHTON A.C. AND St.ALBANS CITY A.C.NOV.30TH. at Ruislip Report and Belgrave results of the four-club cross-country match at Ruislip, won by Belgrave with Charlie Walker second to Hugh Foord. Only ten stalwarts attended this away fixture which was most disappointing and does not encourage the arranging of such matches which are provided to give the opportunity of racing over different types of country to that experienced at our own headquarters. Conditions were first class, and a field of about forty faced the starter. Charlie Walker was soon in the first bunch which was headed by Hugh Foord of Brighton and when seen again at the end of the first lap had established himself in second place some distance behimd Foord. Len Orton, our second claim member from Birchfield, was prominent and Robin Weate was also well placed. Eric Gebbett seemed to be taking an easy start but at the next appearance had worked his way through the field. Robin had dropped a little and Orton seemed far from happy. On the last lap Gebbett had made further progress and Orton had recovered from a bad patch. Fred Paget surprised us by apparently gaining twelve places on the last lap but was later adjudged to have cut about one mile off the course by unwittingly following a rival Polytechnic v. Ilford race which coincided with our course for some distance. We eventually took the team honours with 96 pts. for eight scoring men. Brighton were second with 103 and Finchley third with 169. items.s: CLUB 7 MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP DEC.7TH Report and results of the club 7 miles cross-country championship, won by Eric Gebbett in 36m.47s from Robin Weate, with handicap result. In the absence of Charlie Walker and George Flanagan, the result of this race was very much a matter for speculation. A field of 37 started, including three Essex Beagles men, and a bunch of about twelve runners was soon detached on the first lap, with Eric Gebbett in close attendance. With about two miles to go, J.Masters, who had been forcing the pace for most of the race, fell back rapidly, and was quickly passed by Gebbett, R.Weate and L.Bishop. Once he was in front, a position which always seems to bring out the best in him, Eric quickly established a considerable lead. This he maintained to the end of the race and finished with the highly creditable time of 36m.47s. Our up and coming member Weate, ran extremely well to gain his first place in a Club championship, filling second place, 20 sec. in front of Len Bishop. Good performances came from Steve Charlton, J.Moore and Alan Bishop, whilst new-comer R.Bhatia from Ceylon, astounded most of us by running well to the front and finishing in 8th position. 1 E.Gebbett 36.47 2 R.Weate 37.32 3 L.C.Bishop 37.52 4 J.Moore 38.04 5 E.Short 38.37 6 H.A.Bishop 38.45 7 S.Charlton 38.52 8 R.Bhatia 38.53 9 C.Shippen 39.02 10 J.Masters 39.11 11 J.Heathfield 39.15 12 G.Stevens 39.33 13 J.Edgar 39.56 14 J.Radford 40.11 15 E.M.Bishop 40.14 16 F.Paget 40.15 17 D.Manning 40.27 18 R.Mitchell 40.31 19 R.Glover 40.32 20 D.W.Jones 40.[illegible]0 [?] 21 L.Adams 40.45 22 R.Braine 41.04 23 J.Davies 42.02 24 D.Abbott 42.11 25 C.Dabbs 42.47 26 W.Cousens 42.52 27 G.Davidson 42.57 28 E.S.Stimpson 43.15 29 R.Conway 43.42 30 G.Musselbrook 44.16 31 T.Upperdine 44.16 32 P.Bellenger 46.20 33 J.Baker 46.37 34 R.Hilton 46.48 1st H.A.Bishop (4.15) 34.30 2nd R.Braine (6.30) 34.34 3rd J.Radford (5.15) 34.56 Charlie Walker Charlie Walker absent George Flanagan George Flanagan absent Eric Gebbett Eric Gebbett J. items.sum: Report of the club's 70th anniversary dinner and dance at Barrington House, with presentations to Tom Carter and Stan Vickers.
items.s: CLUB DINNER AND DANCE Report of the club's 70th anniversary dinner and dance at Barrington House, with presentations to Tom Carter and Stan Vickers. Our 70th Anniversary Dinner and Dance, held on 16th November, was undoubtedly a huge success. Due to the hard work of our Social Hon. Secretary, Tom Carter, the function was well supported and the choice of venue, Barrington House, Gresham Street, was a great improvement on last year. Amongst the 230 members and friends who sat down to dinner it was pleasing to see a good number of our younger members. We were pleased to have with us representatives from the governing bodies of Amateur Athletics and after the customary speeches, the President, Syd Roberts, concluded the first half of the evening by presenting a Past President's Plaque to Tom Carter. In the absence of Tommy Green, owing to illness, he also presented the Tommy Green Trophy for the best Club performance to Stan Vickers for his 6th place in the Olympic 20,000 metres walk Dinner was followed by dancing until 11.30p.m. with Bill Lucas, who had earlier carried out the duties of Toastmaster, acting as M.C. items.sum: Field events column reviewing the 1957 season, congratulating Dave Ansell on Maccabia Games selection, welcoming Deszö Audorka and announcing early-season meetings.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP Field events column reviewing the 1957 season, congratulating Dave Ansell on Maccabia Games selection, welcoming Deszö Audorka and announcing early-season meetings. There were no field events notes in the issue of the "Belgravian' just after the track season ended owing to holidays. Normally that contains a review of the season's performances and although a little late we should not forget Percy Porter's fine performances in the hammer, including a 3rd place in the A.A.A. championships and selection as an International reserve.John Powell Jones won the Welsh Shot championship and Charlie (C.R.) Jones put up two fine performances in getting 4th in both Southern and A.A.A. 220 yards hurdles. We had successes in a number of County championships but "Iron Man" Mal Ash had a slightly disappointing season. Those,and one or two others, have a chance of selection for the Empire Games, so we hope they will get down to serious training early, as the team will be chosen immediately after the Southern Championships in June. Congratulations to Dave Ansell, our Captain, on his selection for the British team at the Maccabia Games in Tel-a-Viv. He was 7th in the long jump, 6th in the triple jump and gained a medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay. We should like to extend a special welcome to Deszö Audorka, a very fine International discus thrower from Hungary, and we hope he will be able to show us some of his home form. It was nice to see Malcolm Draper over Christmas. He tells me he has now left hospital and is convalescing - hopes to be home in about two months but unfortunately no athletics for a couple of years. I have already mentioned getting into training early and to help in this Thames Valley Harriers and "The Bels" are putting on meetings on the 8th February and 1st of March respectively for some pre-season competition. The Sward Trophy will be round again on the 10th of May at Chiswick when we hope to turn out our best team to win back the trophy we so narrowly lost last year. The usual Club championships and some handicaps will also be held in the Summer. Details of the Thames Valley meeting can be supplied if anyone is interested. Our own meeting will be held on Saturday 1st March, at Battersea Park, commencing at 1.30 p.m. Events :- Shot Discus Javelin High Jump Long Jump Triple Jump Pole Vault Entries (free) on A.A.A. forms to me not later than 17th Feb. I hope all "Bels" will support our efforts in this meeting. Best wishes to all for the New Year. T.C. Jones. Field Events Honorary Secretary. T.C. Jones T.C. items.label: No. 133
items.sum: Profile of Joseph "Mac" MacDonald, who joined Belgrave in 1938, covering his cross-country, road and London to Brighton record.
items.s: PORTRAIT GALLERY Profile of Joseph "Mac" MacDonald, who joined Belgrave in 1938, covering his cross-country, road and London to Brighton record. Every club has its characters, Belgrave Harriers being no exception. But we don't propose to cover our canvas with the outline of one of those characters whose performances and history are an open book. In 1938, there joined Belgrave, one whom we can only assume was as small, lean and sinewy in those days as he is now. Known to us all as "Mac", Joseph MacDonald has had a dareer as distinguished as many who have been fortunate to be called stars. Under the stern leadership of Footer, Carter and Penny in the immediate post-war years, Mac soon showed he was possessed of great endurance and performed well over the road and country. In 1948 he was in the 3rd team in the Middlesex C.C. championship, 10th in the Kent '20', 3rd team in the Chichester to Portsmouth 16 and 45th in the South of the Thames Junior C.C. race (noted for its large fields). Even better in 1949, he was in our winning South of the Thames Senior team, 59th in the Southern Counties C.C. championship and 5th in the Worthing 5 miles road race. Mac was now established as a road runner and between 1951 and 1953 won the Club Marathon Championship and was placed 2nd and 3rd. But his greatest feats have been in the London to Brighton 52½ miles race where, when twice in dire straits with still a considerable distance to be covered, he has forced himself on in order not to let his team down. Altogether he has been in one third, one second and one winning team in this race in 1952, 1955 and 1956 respectively. His attendance at road and cross-country events and at training sessions has been an example to all. Week after week at the Duke of York's at Sloane Square, he would come tearing in at the last moment on his bicycle (he wasn't such a plutocrat in those days) and oblivious to the abuse hurled at him by those ready to leave, would hastily don his gear and with feet pattering loud enough to disturb half Sloane Square, would join the pack. Good-hearted and generous, it was often barley sugars all round when sweets were rationed; Mac it seemed had relations who didn't indulge. He has been with us years and will still be performing well for many to come. Our London to Brighton team can always rely on him. A true Belgravian, whose performances have so often gone unseen except by the few on the long lonely roads; we are proud to put them on record. items.sum: Letter from the new Track Secretary, D.M. Shepherd, asking members to answer fixture postcards and support the club championships on 14th June.
items.s: FROM THE TRACK SECRETARY Letter from the new Track Secretary, D.M. Shepherd, asking members to answer fixture postcards and support the club championships on 14th June. For the first time I have taken on the task of Track Secretary and I am looking forward to a very successful year for all those members of the Club who are interested in track running We have a very full programme before us, and it should give all of you plenty of racing. Arranging this programme has occasioned us a great deal of hard work, so you will be expected to co-operate by replying immediately to all postcards that may be sent to you, stating whether or not you can take part in a particular fixture. By so doing you will be making our task much easier. Try to make the coming track season a success by doing your best to turn out for the Club, and by remembering that you are part of a team and not just an individual. If I, Bob Taylor, Clive Shippen or Jim Heathfield can help in any way do not hesitate to write to us or see us personally, and we will do our best for you. If you do not help me and the job falls down, through lack of co-operation it will be no good crying about it. Note especially the date of the Club championships. They will be held on Saturday 14th of June in the evening, and will start at approximately 6.00 p.m. We want to make a special effort this year to have a really first class meeting, and once again it will be up to the competitors, that is yourselves, to SUPPORT these championships. I, on my part, will make sure that the track is there, that the officials are there and that the cups and trophies are also there. Make it a real day and bring the family. Yours sincerely. D.M. Shepherd. D.M. Shepherd D.M. Shepherd. Track Secretary Bob Taylor Bob Taylor Clive Shippen Clive Shippen Jim Heathfield Jim Heathfield Club Championships

items.sum: Road running notes by H.A. Bishop urging training and entries for the 1958 long-distance season, with a list of the main events.
items.s: ROAD RUNNING NOTES. Road running notes by H.A. Bishop urging training and entries for the 1958 long-distance season, with a list of the main events. With the long distance road running season barely two months away it is to be hoped that all distance runners are now getting down to serious training. There are numerous events, ranging from 10 to 53 miles, so that all tastes can be catered for. I would particularly like to see a very strong Belgrave entry in each of the two main events, namely the Polytechnic marathon and our own Open 20 miles race, both of which carry a Club championship in conjunction. Scarcely less important is the Finchley 20, which this year incorporates the Southern 20 miles championship. This race presents a good opportunity to secure a Southern standard, as the course is easy and the modest time of 2 hrs. 5 min. should be within everybody's capabilities. There is, of course, no A.A.A. standard for this distance. Southern marathon standard ( 2 hrs.50 mins.) is a trifle more difficult, but on the flat Windsor to Chiswick route it shouldn't present too much trouble provided weather conditions are reasonable. The A.A.A. standard of 2 hrs.35 mins. is a tough proposition on any course. In many distance events, the promotors stipulate that team runners must make individual entries, and I would suggest that this be done in all cases to avoid any possibility of being left out of a team. If you are not one of the recognised distance men and feel that you would like to take part in a certain race or races just drop me a line and I will include you in the team, assuming, of course, that we have a team going to that particular event. Wishing you all a successful season with not too many blisters. H.A. Bishop, 13, Woodside Way, Long Lane, Croydon, Surrey Below is a list of the main long distance events for 1958. items.sum: Editorial on the start of the track and road season, the Battersea Park field events meeting, Fred Stone's police bravery award, a disappointing flu-hit cross country season and the success of the walkers under Jack Goswell.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial on the start of the track and road season, the Battersea Park field events meeting, Fred Stone's police bravery award, a disappointing flu-hit cross country season and the success of the walkers under Jack Goswell. Dear Fellow Members, By the time this edition is published, the track and road season will be with us and it is to be hoped that the Winter has not been spent in idleness by those wishing to do well in these spheres. Our field events men are already hard at it as witness our successful open meeting at Battersea Park on March 2nd. This event does great credit to its organisers and it is a valuable contribution, giving performers competition during the close season. Our old friend, P.C. Fred Stone, was seen by many on a television programme recently when receiving an award in recognition of his bravery during police service. Harry Evans, as sprightly as ever, also appeared on the programme to recount some tales of their younger days. We needn't be too disappointed with the cross country season, for like so many other clubs we were victims of a flu-ridden Winter. It cannot be too strongly emphasized, however, that a season over the country demands both sufficient groundwork and sensible racing. So many seem to forget that the real tests come after Christmas; to feel race-weary when the new year begins is fatal. Likewise it is equally fatal to expect to commence one's season in January with the Southern and National in mind. Under such circumstances it is not possible to produce top performances in both events. Our walkers continue winning in merciless fashion and we must not lose sight of that great driving force behind them, Jack Goswell. He must be the Stampfl of the walking world in his ability to bring out the best in his men. To Eric Hall and Stan Vickers, who have never walked better we offer our congratulations. It may sound fantastic but Eric, now one of our "greats" won a 2 mile walk handicap in 1950, off 650 yards! So go to it, you novices. Fred Stone P.C. items.h: MATCH v. MITCHAM, MET. POLICE AND GUILDFORD & GODALMING A.C. at BANSTEAD. DEC.28TH
items.sum: Report of a four-club cross country match at Banstead won narrowly by Belgrave, led home by John Davies in 8th.
items.s: MATCH v. MITCHAM, MET. POLICE AND GUILDFORD & GODALMING A.C. at BANSTEAD. DEC.28TH Report of a four-club cross country match at Banstead won narrowly by Belgrave, led home by John Davies in 8th. Out of our terrific numerical strength of cross country runners we could only muster thirteen, including three juniors, for this away fixture. The venue is set in the midst of Surrey's grand scenery and provides a complete change to the normal terrain over which we run. I have little doubt that all who took part had an enjoyable afternoon. John Davies, who has been a regular participant in cross country fixtures this year, led home the Belgrave contingent in 8th place, closely followed by a pack of Belgravians in 10th, 11th, 12th, 14th, 15th, 17th and 18th positions. This good bunching enabled us to secure a narrow win in the team race, with Mitcham second, Met. Police third and Guildford fourth. Ken Jones was performing for the Police and ran well to finish fourth in the individual placings. Bob Glover, a strong runner, deserves special mention - he is continually improving and without doubt will greatly assist our teams before many seasons are over - stick to it Bob! 1st Belgrave (8,10,11,12,14,15) 70 pts 2nd Mitcham (1,2,5,19,21,24) 72 " 3rd Met.Police (4,6,9,13,20,28) 80 " 4th Guildford & Godalming (3,7,16,22,23,25) 96 " John Davies John Davies led home the Belgrave contingent in 8th place Ken Jones Ken Jones 4th Bob Glover Bob Glover singled out as a strong, improving runner Banstead Surrey Mitcham Met. items.label: No. 134
items.h: SURREY COUNTY C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP AT REIGATE. JAN.4TH
items.sum: Report of the Surrey county cross country championship at Reigate, where Belgrave finished fourth behind Herne Hill, South London and Walton, with D. Baulch the first Belgrave man in 11th.
items.s: SURREY COUNTY C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP AT REIGATE. JAN.4TH Report of the Surrey county cross country championship at Reigate, where Belgrave finished fourth behind Herne Hill, South London and Walton, with D. Baulch the first Belgrave man in 11th. This race was held at the same venue as the South of the Thames Junior in November and the course consisted of a mixture of grassland, firm paths and hills, some of which were very steep.It could well be described as a good sporty course.The finishing time indicated a distance well in excess of the scheduled seven miles which produced some grumblings from the competitors, especially those whose training had previously been of a sketchy nature. It would seem that we are doomed to take team positions outside the first three in this race for some years to come unless we can split the strength of South London and Herne Hill and the recent rise to power of Walton A.C. Indeed, we have not won this event since 1952 nor been placed since 1955. Only Baulch and Gebbett ran true to form and finished in positions which deserve any special mention. Baulch especially was in fine fettle to finish 11th behind such names as Firth, Caulder, Barrett, Towl, Maynard, Clark and Driver, all of whom are in international class in one sphere or another. Dave was indeed unlucky to miss his selection for the County team but should fare better next year. Eric Gebbett eventually finished 20th after having been up to 15th at one stage - it seems strange to have to report that the extra distance was his downfall.Charlie Walker in 33rd place was very disappointing - perhaps he should not forecast his running before the race - it always seems to be fatal. Len Bishop and Eddie Short should have been at least ten places higher than their 42nd and 43rd, and Peter Hitchcock should also have been better positioned than 52nd. It is obvious that we have the talent but it is not put to the best use when major races are run. Instead of rising to the occasion we fall further and further from grace. Do we do enough training to keep up with modern conditions? 1st Herne Hill H. (4,5,6,8,12,16) 51 pts. 2nd South London H. (1,7,22,23,27,29) 109 " 3rd Walton A.C. items.h: MATCH v. ORPINGTON A.C., ISLE OF SHEPPEY AND OLD CROYDONIANS AT ORPINGTON JAN.11TH
items.sum: Report of a poorly supported cross country match at Orpington in which Belgrave, with only four runners, finished second to Orpington.
items.s: MATCH v. ORPINGTON A.C., ISLE OF SHEPPEY AND OLD CROYDONIANS AT ORPINGTON JAN.11TH Report of a poorly supported cross country match at Orpington in which Belgrave, with only four runners, finished second to Orpington. The Cross Country Secretary sent out numerous cards directing runners to this fixture but the nett result was a turnout of four which was extremely disappointing and an insult to our hosts. The race took place over good grassland over a distance of five miles and Robin Weate and J.Dooley ran together to finish second and third. Gerry Lines made one of his rare appearances and showed welcome form to finish 9th. Musselbrook rose to the occasion in answering the card sent to him by appearing in person to complete our team in 17th position. Orpington took the team honours with 22 pts., Bels..were second with 31, Sheppey scored 44 and Old Croydonians amassed 75. On the whole an enjoyable afternoon out for the few stalwarts who supported this fixture. It should of course be mentioned that we had another away race against Westminster Bank on this day which split our forces but nevertheless there were many of our members who stayed away from both. items.s: WALKING NOTES Walking notes covering the Essex Beagles youths and juniors race won by Nic Milsum, E.A. Smith's third in the London Business Houses 7 miles, a match win over Met. Police at Hayes, and Stan Vickers' record win in the Metropolitan Police open 7 mile walk at Imber Court. We entered a team in the Essex Beagles open 3¾ miles youths and juniors race. Nic Milsum walked very well to win the race in 28.56 and Bryan Cornish was 8th in 31.18. Unfortunately we lost both Terry Clark and John Knifton who came under the judge's ban when in 2nd and 4th positions thus ruining any chances of winning the team race. The same day (Jan.4th) E.A.Smith finished third in the London Business Houses 7 mile championship in 55.52. We also had a match versus Met.Police at "The Warren" Hayes and in a field of eighteen Stan Vickers was first home in 56.05. R.D.McMullen was second and R.C.Hall third. Scoring eight a side we won with 43½ pts. to 93½. On Jan 11th at Imber Court the Metropolitan Police held their open 7 mile walk and in a field of 195 Stan Vickers led for the whole way to win in the record time of 50.14 which was 78 secs. faster than the previous best. With Eric Hall 4th, R.D.McMullen 16th and George Checkley 19th we easily won the team race from Met.W.C. and Highgate. It was very pleasing to see the large number of Club supporters stationed around the course - their presence was well rewarded. items.s: CLUB 10 MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP (MACHER SHIELD) JAN.25TH Report and result of the club 10 miles cross country championship for the Macher Shield, won by Charlie Walker, with Bob Plummer taking the handicap. This year's race,held on a cold damp day, ran true to form with Charlie Walker, who always performs so well over our own courses, the winner by the comfortable margin of 47 seconds. Dave Baulch took second place, 53 seconds ahead of Eric Gebbett who had earlier in the season won the seven miles championship. This was the order which had been maintained almost throughout the race and the fact that, for the second year, the course was inadvertently shortened by missing out the lap of the starting field in the middle of the race, obviously made no difference to the result. The back markers in the handicap could well complain, for if the full distance had been covered there is little doubt that Walker and Moore would have been among the prizes. John Moore (the second), in his first season with us, has made his mark upon us and will soon be taking a leading place in our races and should bolster up our teams both on track and country. His fourth place in this event was well earned, for he has been a keen performer since he joined us. Archie Bedford returned for one of his rare visits and, by finishing fifth, proved he still has the capacity to gain a place in our first teams. Eddie Short ran well to take sixth place and that "little potterer" Joe Dooley followed close on his heels with Jim Heathfield, only a few yards behind. Bob Plummer, better known for his exploits over the marathon distance, took advantage of the handicapper's generosity to win the handicap by a good margin. items.sum: Report and result of the South of the Thames senior cross country championship held from Belgrave Hall, won by Blackheath Harriers, with Belgrave 9th and George Flanagan 13th.
items.s: SOUTH OF THAMES SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP FEB.1ST Report and result of the South of the Thames senior cross country championship held from Belgrave Hall, won by Blackheath Harriers, with Belgrave 9th and George Flanagan 13th. This race was held from Belgrave Hall in honour of Les Cohen who this year is President of the South of the Thames Cross Country Association. He must have been proud of the efficient manner in which this event was organised and our thanks go out to Arthur Whitehead who took all the responsibility for course marking and the provision of starting and finishing pens upon his experienced shoulders. The number of barring clauses in this event precluded the fielding of our strongest team, but on paper our lads, with a mixture of experience and youthful exuberance, appeared to have a chance of a place. Unfortunately we were again to be disappointed as we could finish no better than 9th in the team race with the mammoth score of 461 pts. George Flanagan was the only one of our runners who excelled himself and he should be pleased with thirteenth position. John Moore, by finishing 52nd, gained good experience in a large field and Robin Weate, in his first year with us, showed that he is possessed of more than his fair share of pluck to finish 88th. Robin, still a junior, always gives of his best and is a great asset to us - with regular and correct training he should follow in the footsteps of that courageous little man, Bert Footer, who did so much for Belgrave in the years preceding the last war. Bob Glover, also in his first season, improves with every outing and in finishing 111th can be said to have performed well and should benefit from this experience. Ken Jones, running in the colours of the Metropolitan Police A.C. ran very well to take 33rd place and will be a tower of strength in these races when we have his services. items.h: SOUTHERN COUNTIES SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP at Parliament Hill Feb.15th
items.sum: Report and result of the Southern Counties senior cross country championship at Parliament Hill, won by South London Harriers, with Belgrave a disappointing 9th, plus notes on the Southern youths and junior races where George Flanagan was 5th.
items.s: SOUTHERN COUNTIES SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP at Parliament Hill Feb.15th Report and result of the Southern Counties senior cross country championship at Parliament Hill, won by South London Harriers, with Belgrave a disappointing 9th, plus notes on the Southern youths and junior races where George Flanagan was 5th. A return to the course over which the National was held last year saw one of the biggest fields ever set off on the long trek of nine miles over hilly grassland with a fair proportion of mud and slush. Toward the end of the first of the three laps Eric Gebbett was our first scorer way back in 49th place followed closely by Charlie Walker 55th. Then followed a string of runners before we again saw a Belgrave vest filled by Eddie Short who had John Moore and Jumbo Masters close on his heels, all of them in the 130's. Pete Hitchcock, Clive Shippen and Len Bishop were next, in the 170's while the rest of our men were back in the 200's. The next view of the field was soon after the first lap had ended, and Walker had moved up to Gebbett and Short and Moore had also progressed about fifteen places and were running well. Masters was making very heavy weather of it and was slipping back steadily, Hitchcock and Shippen were 152nd and 167th respectively with Len Bishop and D.Baulch in close attendance. At the conclusion of the second lap Walker had left Gebbett and was now 44th but was having great difficulty in making any further progress. Although Gebbett was slipping back gradually, Short and Moore were still making up ground and were now 103rd and 104th. Our other men however, were making little or no improvement with the exception of J.Dooley who had started very slowly and was now beginning his late excursion through the field. On the last lap Moore made up another ten places and Hitchcock put in a good run to move up nearly thirty places. Dooley seemed to enjoy himself at this stage and must have passed about fifty runners in the last three miles. The others seemed to have got themselves well bogged down. The final count gave us ninth place with the astronomical score of 591 points, which must have been our lowest place and highest score for a good many years. The impression one gets from this fiasco is that most if not all of our runners are short of the type of training needed to keep pace with the leading performers. On examining the final positions one cannot fail to notice how many athletes, possessed of far less ability than our lads, finished well up the field and assisted their clubs to secure good places - the moral is obvious. Result :- Individuals :- Also held at Parliament Hill on the same day were the Southern Youths and Junior championships. Our juniors ran very well to finish fourth in the team race. An outstanding performance was that of George Flanagan in being placed fifth, a performance which qualifies him for a Junior Honours Badge. Another good run was that of Robin Weate who was 21st. In the youths race Belgrave were 10th.The only other news we have is that C.Thompson was 26th and J.Thresher 48th. 1st South London Harriers 136 pts. 2nd Thames Valley Harriers 142 " 3rd Woodford Green A.C. 206 " 9th Belgrave Harriers 591 " 47 C.W. items.s: COUNTY 10 MILES WALKING CHAMPIONSHIPS - FEB.22ND. Report on the county 10 miles walking championships: Eric Hall won Surrey with Belgrave taking the team race, the Club (as Cadogan A.C.) was second team in Middlesex, and Stan Vickers won Kent for the third year running. The splendid performances of our walkers in county championships gives every promise of Belgrave repeating last year's record of winning all three major R.W.A. titles. Again those two great ambassadors of the sport, Eric Hall and Stan Vickers, retained their titles in a convincing manner. A feat probably never equalled by any other club was that of ten Belgrave walkers gaining their county colours. Surrey at Walton-on-Thames. A splendid race was won in immaculate style by Eric Hall who was just over one minute ahead of Dave McMullen.Then followed three other Belgravians which meant that the team race was won with the minimum score of ten points. It is interesting to note that our"B" team finished in third position which gives a startling indication of Club strength. 1st Belgrave "A" 10 pts. 2nd Surrey W.C."A" 39 pts. 3rd Belgrave"B" Middlesex at Enfield A full team plus two individuals, as Cadogan A.C., represented the Club, and right well the performed to finish second team to Metropolitan Walking Club, beating Highgate, Polytechnic and many other fancied clubs in the process. A particularly fine effort was that of Ted Smith in finishing fourth and George Checkley sixth. Kent at Hayes This might be described as Stan Vickers benefit, which he won for the third year in succession (not running!), walking completely on his own, with the ease and style which have become the standards whereby all others are judged. items.sum: Report of a 7½ mile cross-country match at Wimbledon which Belgrave won with 46 points despite moved marking flags sending Clive Shippen off course.
items.s: MATCH v. FINCHLEY H. & ORPINGTON A.C. FEB.22ND at Wimbledon Report of a 7½ mile cross-country match at Wimbledon which Belgrave won with 46 points despite moved marking flags sending Clive Shippen off course. About forty runners faced the starter for a race of 7½ miles in which there was a great preponderance of Belgrave Harriers including a number of old stalwarts. At the end of the first lap Clive Shippen was leading with Moore and Short well in attendance. A quick check showed that we were well in the lead and should have no difficulty in holding our position. Unfortunately a number of small boys on the Common thought otherwise and on the second lap the marking flags were found to have been moved with the result that Clive Shippen went well off course and was left with too much ground to make up to regain his early lead. John Moore and Eddie Short soon discovered their mistake and all was well once more but the whole character of the race had been changed. Nevertheless we gained a comfortable win, scoring seven a side, with 46 points against 82 by Finchley and 103 by Orpington. items.s: GOSPORT OPEN SEVEN MILES WALK.MARCH 1ST Report of the Gosport Open Seven Miles Walk, won by Eric Hall by 14 seconds with Belgrave taking the team award, followed by an account of a Sunday stroll from Croydon the next morning. We sent a small team down for this new venture, and after a rough sea crossing we were not quite so sure we should have bothered. After being "Security Cleared" we changed in a barracks, no autograph hunters were allowed just in case we looked like volunteers. The course itself was flat and Stan Vickers soon showed the way, followed by a large of local lads. Soon the pace began to tell and at two miles Eric Hall had moved through and was breathing very heavily down Stan's neck with Norman Read just behind. Nick Milsum had a bad time, but fought back well to regain lost ground near the finish. At four miles Eric moved away and Stan fell back to third, but not for long however, as over the last mile he closed right up again and Eric just got home by 14 seconds. Ray Hall had a great fight all the way and used bluff to finish 8th. Terry Clark was always handy and he was followed by Joe Coleman who took first veteran's prize. Nick Milsum was third in the handicap and of course we won the team award - a very successful pot hunt. Harry Shields made his mark by leading others astray on the pretext of having tea - result - we had four minutes to swim 200 yards, sprint half a mile and jump six feet. It was a good job we were fit or we'd have missed that train. 1st Belgrave H. 16 pts. 2nd Trowbridge 55 " 3rd Gosport 69 " The following morning six of the above considered themselves fit enough to go strolling. At precisely 0936 we left Croydon led by Harry Shields (shortly to explore Birkenhead) and a steady pace was maintained for six or seven miles by which time we were above the snow line. The leading bunch must have had skis, as they moved away very fast, led by "Sherpa" Clark, followed by Stan and Nick Milsum. The inevitable happened, and when Harry took a sun shot we found that the intrepid trio were hell bent for somewhere about a mile off course. Much signalling resulted and they eventually rejoined the main group in time to buy refreshments. Stan was by now sporting Club colours - he was looking alternately purple and yellow! We ascended the south Col of the downs shortly after this and made good progress to our next camp, where we waited for one straggler, who must remain nameless, then after dropping Terry Clark and Stan, the survivors pushed on over Hayes Common where Harry deviated too much to the right and was lost without trace. The two Halls were left to complete this epic, incident packed march on their own No matter what you have done on the previous day, a Sunday stroll with the Boys is the best tonic you can have. A. items.s: BELGRAVE OPEN FIELD EVENTS MEETING. MARCH 1ST Report of the club's second winter open field events meeting, with 82 individual entrants, noting the discus second place of D[illegible]szo Audorka and thanking the officials. Our second Winter Meeting was better supported than last year and even more successful. There was an entry of 82 individuals and an event entry of 128. This included some of the best performers in the country and a contingent from Cambridge University. The day was not an ideal one perhaps, but after the snowy weather in the early part of the week we were lucky indeed to be able to carry the meeting through. The javelin, perhaps, suffered most from the conditions and we really must try and persuade the L.C.C. to put down a cinder approach. Better support could have come from our own members, although we were represented in all the events except the Shot. It was pleasing to see two of our javelin throwers getting in the first six despite this being our weakest event. Bill Couzens was disappointing, especially after his good performance in the T.V.H. meeting.He is really still a novice as far as the javelin is concerned but is showing promise and must improve during the summer. Our best performer was undoubtedly D[illegible]szo Audorka with a fine throw in the discus for second place after a neck and neck battle with the winner who only widened the margin between them to four feet with his last throw. We hope to see him doing some 160's or more in the summer. Our thanks are due to the Surrey County Judges, Messrs. Reed, Fairfoul and Reeve and to Mr.E.F.Housden, the old pole vault Champion, for their assistance, together with the Club members who came along and particularly to Dick Savage who acted as Referee. items.s: NATIONAL C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS. BIRKENHEAD MARCH 8TH Report of the National cross-country championships at Birkenhead covering Belgrave's youths (12th team), seniors (15th team, Pat Newell 39th) and juniors (16th team). An unusually small band of runners and officials availed themselves of the special transport put on by British Railways for this the premier cross country event of the year. Event one, the youths race over 3 miles started in bright sunshine, most unexpected after the violent snow showers which greeted our arrival.In a large field, Arthur Penny's youngsters performed quite creditably, our first man home being Thresher in 77th place.Having partaken in a schools race the day before, Eric Penny can be said to have run well to finish 127th. Other positions:- C. Thompson 105 T. Hart 108 D. Crooks 124 Team result :- Belgrave H. 12th,414 pts. 53 teams closed in. The senior event, always a race to stir a feeling of awe in the spectator, was soon seen to be an S.L.H. "benefit", for they had three men in six at one stage. What is it about men like Firth, Driver, Pirie and company which enables them always to strike the front within half a mile or so? Pat Newell, running in his first cross country race this season, clung tenaciously to a good start and was always placed around the forty mark. He eventually finished 39th, ahead of international Harry Hicks and many other performers of high rank. Next man was Charlie Walker, 77th, an improvement on recent form, with ever consistant Eric Gebbett 134th. A special mention must be made of Clive Shippen who has been short of training. He put in as much work as possible between the Southern and this race and reaped the benefits. To finish 175th in this field was no mean performance. The rest of our men finished outside the two-hundreds. In the team race we were 15th and the only consolation that can be got from this is that Birchfield were 16th - how are the mighty fallen! To establish a lead of almost 200 yds by two miles and then coast home from a good class field was a meritorious performance. George Flanagan seemed unable to get going. Whilst Geoff Stevens 118th, and K.Miller 1[illegible]6th improved on their Southern running our other lads found the pace too hot. No one was disgraced, however, and in them we have some good material for the future.
