items.sum: Lap-by-lap report of the club's 8th annual 20-mile road race, won by W. 'Digger' Pawsey, with Len Bishop first Belgrave man in 6th and Belgrave second team to T.V.H. Results list two runners at 28th as printed.
items.s: THE 8th ANNUAL BELGRAVE '20' - 15th AUG. Lap-by-lap report of the club's 8th annual 20-mile road race, won by W. 'Digger' Pawsey, with Len Bishop first Belgrave man in 6th and Belgrave second team to T.V.H. Results list two runners at 28th as printed. This was another event to suffer through fixture congestion - the Liverpool marathon and the Enschide event being held the same day. Despite this, a good field of 73 competitors faced the Deputy Mayor of Wimbledon (Councillor A.E.Ayres) to await the start in conditions summarised on the result sheet as "fine and warm, with a cooling breeze." After the first of the four 5 mile laps W.'Digger' Pawsey, of Mitcham A.C. and Brian Cooke of Haltemprice R.R.C., were almost a minute clear of the field. Then came Len Bishop in 3rd. place Eric 9th, Bob Glover (coerced into running by Ken Stimpson) 10th!, with Alan Bishop, Joe Dooley and Bob Plummer running well together in 14th position - 1 min.49 secs. down on the leaders. At the end of the second lap it was clear that the first two places had been booked by Pawsey and Cooke, but Lennie was hanging onto third place despite nagging attention from Hopcroft (TVH) and Shave (HHH), whilst brother Eric had moved up to 8th. Bob Glover was back to 12th with Alan Bishop, Joe Dooley and Reg Plummer hard on his heels. At this stage the Bels. and the Valley were neck and neck in the team race and excitement was mounting. Necks were craned to watch the runners approach 15 miles in the hope that Len had established third place, but unfortunately he had not had a good time this lap for Hopcroft and Shave had well and truly dropped him, whilst Elderfield (TVH) had also moved ahead by some 23 secs. Eric was still 8th and Alan now 12th fighting it out with Davies (TVH) and Paxton (HHH). Bob Glover was fading badly and was now a further 1½ mins. down, having been caught by Joe Dooley and Bob Plummer. Ken Stimpson, Geoff Pearson and Pete Mathews were 23rd, 25th and 26th. when the fifty-six competitors remaining went out for the final lap. Pawsey was a comfortable winner in the 2nd. fastest time ever recorded, 1hr 51:06 and Cooke's 1hr 52:12 had been bettered on only three occasions. Len Bishop was first man home for the Bels. finishing 6th, the same 23 secs behind Elderfield as he was with 5 miles to go. Eric Bishop had a most uncomfortable last lap owing to stomach trouble and dropped five places, however, the team result wasn't affected and the Bishop brothers were still our first three men home. Thus enabling Sam Ferris to write "Equally popular were the performances of the amazing Bishop brothers (Bishop A.C.) who placed Belgrave 2nd......" Joe Dooley finished strongly to finish 14th, two up on Bob Plummer and six up on Geoff Pearson, who had moved through from 35th with the most even-paced run of the day recording lap times of 31:20, 31:29, 31:46 and 31:51. Ken Stimpson also ran exceptionally well to finish 21st. Bob Glover came almost to a standstill on his last lap (37:02!), but still recorded 2hr 07:57 and took 2nd place in the handicap for good measure. Pete Mathews also had an encouraging run while Arthur Penstone was another last lap sufferer. T.V.H., won on superior staying power but with 10 in 29 the Bels. could be justly proud of their performance. The expert organisation of Bill Bird, and the assistance of Arthur Whitehead were most successfull and greatly appreciated in making this event a milestone in the road-running calendar. 1.W.Pawsey (Mitcham) 1.51:06 2.B.Cooke (Haltemprice) 1.52:12 3.G.Hopcroft (T.V.H.) 1.55:42 ......... 6.L.C.Bishop 1.58:27 11.H.A.Bishop 2.00:34 13.E.M.Bishop 2.01:59 14.J.Dooley 2.03:00 16.R.G.Plummer 2.04:16 20.G.Pearson 2.06:26 23.K.Stimpson 2.06:45 28.R.Glover 2.07:57 28.P.Mathews 2.11:32 29.J.McDonald 2.13:17 31.A.Penstone 2.17:28 39.W.Fairfield 2.23:22 46.R.A.Conway 2.32:27 1.T.V.H. items.sum: Tribute to Colin Collis on his retirement from competition after a comeback that ended with eighth place in the Polytechnic Marathon.
items.s: COLIN COLLIS Tribute to Colin Collis on his retirement from competition after a comeback that ended with eighth place in the Polytechnic Marathon. Colin has finally decided to call it a day! This great-hearted club-man who fought so hard to reach the top has now had to give way to the effects of further injury, a new home and the calls of family life. He had already retired once but the lure of athletics proved too great to resist so he began the the long trek back to fitness culminating in a Polytechnic Marathon performance which brought him home in eighth place, ahead of many better known rivals. Colin was no natural athlete. In his early days he was frequently seen amongst the tailenders, but eventually made the grade by sheer hard work. Many of our members would do well to follow his example. We have lost a valuable competitor but are sure to have retained a keen supporter, whose constant contact with the young might well reap dividends for Belgrave. Colin Collis COLIN COLLIS retired; 8th in Polytechnic Marathon Polytechnic Marathon

CLUB 6 MILE CHAMPIONSHIP - 19th AUG.
The "TOM CARTER" Cup
items.sum: Report and results of the club 6-mile championship for the Tom Carter Cup, won by Pat Newell in 30:46, with results of a 300 yards handicap and a junior 880 yards held the same evening.
items.s: CLUB 6 MILE CHAMPIONSHIP - 19th AUG. The "TOM CARTER" Cup Report and results of the club 6-mile championship for the Tom Carter Cup, won by Pat Newell in 30:46, with results of a 300 yards handicap and a junior 880 yards held the same evening. On a hot summer evening, and on a bone hard track Pat Newell the defending champion, and fifteen challengers faced the starter. After only one lap 'Glimpy' Jones and Dereck Crooks were a good twenty yards up on Pat and going as though they were after an international vest! Their lead was, however, gradually cut down and on the third lap the leading bunch was comprised of Newell, Walker, Moore and Bedford. During the second mile Pat broke away and was never again headed, while Don Maclean made one of his typical surges through the field to join the battle for 2nd. place with the other three. At three miles Charlie, only just recovering from injury, found the pace too hot while Mac had the opposite view and gradually pulled clear to isolate himself in 2nd place. Meanwhile John Moore and Archie Bedford were battling it out shoulder to shoulder and remained that way til the last half-mile, when John, who had almost been dropped a couple of minutes earlier, drew away to take 3rd. place. Pat, with no one to trouble him, slowed up appreciably in the latter stages but ran out a comfortable winner in 30min 46secs. Don Maclean was untroubled for the greater part and ran a very well-judged race. It was very good to see Gordan Biscoe and Mike Stearman out again, as it was to see such an encouraging performance from John Hilton. RESULT: The first two were inside first-class standard, with third and fourth inside second-class. Other events held during the evening were a 300 yards handicap in which Charlie Jones,off 2 yards, narrowly failed to run right through the field. An A.A.A. vest should soon come Gerry's way and could well be followed by even higher honours. Pat Newell and Charlie Dabbs produced two personal best performances in the three miles, finishing 3rd and 5th with 14:14.4 and 14:22.4 respectively. These times become first and second in the Club's season's rankings - an excellent performance. Dereck McCorquindale won the shot with a putt of 46ft 4½ins, whilest Dave Ansell secured third place in the long-jump with 21'4¾". In a very close 100 yds finish Sylvan Deane was 4th in 10.5 secs; and to complete the picture Eric Smith was sixth in the 2 mile walk. Despite our outstanding performances we relinquished our hold on the "W.J.PEPPER" Memorial Trophy, partly due no doubt to our having no Junior performers, and Eric Hall being unable to defend his 2 mile walk title, through injury. items.sum: Review, signed T.C.J., of Belgrave's 1959 field events season, naming the leading jumpers and throwers and appealing for fuller teams; it starts on page 27 and ends at the foot of page 12.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS REVIEW. Review, signed T.C.J., of Belgrave's 1959 field events season, naming the leading jumpers and throwers and appealing for fuller teams; it starts on page 27 and ends at the foot of page 12. The past season has been but a moderate one for whilst we have some good performers we have insufficient depth even up to a moderate standard. The main event for our men "The Sward", has been fully reported in an earlier edition. Injuries and illness beset us then and we have had a recurrence throughout the season, and more often than not have not turned out full teams in Trophy matches or even, to our disgrace, in our own home inter-club matches. Derek McCorquindale has no doubt been our best class performer. His new Club Championship best with the Shot of 49'9" and later the same day a 51'4" to win the Bucks Championships were two of his best efforts; he was also selected for A.A.A. teams. Dave Ansell has had quite a good season, attaining a place in the Middlesex Championships and winning the Maccabi European Championship with 22ft odd. He, Jim McGrath,and in the late season Reg Chamberlain (just back from the Forces) represented us in most of the Long Jumps. Jim McGrath is another "Iron Man" of the calibre of Mal Ash. His efforts in two, three or even four events at matches has been of inestimable help and in true Belgrave Spirit. He tells me that he has not been so fit as in some years,but gave a creditable show in finsihing 10th in the A.A.A. Decathlon with 4,405 points; just missing Standard. Pole Vault is really perhaps his best event, although he has run well over the 120 yards Hurdles. It was unfortunate that in this event Robin Tolson was unable to overcome an early season injury, and was never able to race. John Sams has done virtually nothing hurdlewise, except the Sward, but Pat Fox ran one or two reasonable 440's as second string to Charlie Jones. Norman Caves's early effort of 46'5" in the Triple Jump gave promise of great things but he suffered injury and it was not until late in the season that he came back with performances nearing his best. He again won the Beds and Hunts Championship. Dave Ansell has supported well in this event and Brian Jones, a new member, shows promise. Charlie Jones has also performed creditably in the triple and long-jump, but his hurdling seems to have gone to pieces; although in the Fulham Borough meeting a win in the 220 lows with 25.7 secs showed something nearer his true standard. In the High-Jump we have been really weak but perhaps Alan Stanborough will get back to his true 6 ft plus form next year. Jim McGrath, Dave Rasey and Norman Caves have all reached 5'6". The Javelin and Discus were weak events. John Ware has shown small improvement with a personal best of 169'10½" gaining second place in the Vancover Trophy, but is inconsistent. Bill Couzens found that Army life does not make for much improvement, more particularly perhaps because he has not been able to compete regularly; although he has thrown 169 ft and over in practice. Deszo Andorka has virtually had no Discus competition owing to examinations but we hope next year he will be able to get back his true form. Our other performers are all below 120 feet. Percy Porter, in the Hammer, has not reached his best but it is good to see Jock Whyte improving, winning the Middlesex only to have a bad day in the Scottish Championships. Ted Arnold has also shown a small improvement. Our Juniors seem non-existent, although Mike Smithers and Alan Blackett have appeared in the Jumps- but where are the throwers? The same might be said for the Youths, except for Dereck Wade in the Jumps. Norman Dewberry has now taken over as Secretary and I hope you will all give him your earnest support to make the Club what it should be and ensure we turn out full teams next year. We can win or help to win most matches and Trophies just by turning out a full team. We hold our Open Winter Field Events on 5th March 1960, when I hope all will turn out. /cont foot P.12 P.27. Field Events contd. Generally a disappointing season. Even the Club Championships' entries were sparse, and for Handicaps worse. One last note. I would like to thank everyone for their support particularly those who acted as Judges and Marksmen. T.C.J. items.h: SURREY COUNTY ROAD RELAYS - WOKING - 12th SEPT
items.sum: Report of the Surrey County Road Relays at Woking, where Belgrave were sixth in the new youths' relay and fifth in the senior 6 x 3 miles, with a closing note signed W.E.L. and an editor's reply.
items.s: SURREY COUNTY ROAD RELAYS - WOKING - 12th SEPT Report of the Surrey County Road Relays at Woking, where Belgrave were sixth in the new youths' relay and fifth in the senior 6 x 3 miles, with a closing note signed W.E.L. and an editor's reply. The afternoon's proceedings opened with the newly instituted relay for Youths, over a two mile course. Our four runners were Roy Bagley, Mike Smithers, Eddie Gaze and Eric Penny in that order. Seven teams faced the starter and at the end of the first leg we were fifth with Mitcham A.C. in the lead nearly half a minute ahead - Roy had run well but seemed to finish with too much in hand probably through lack of experience of this type of racing. Mike Smithers was unfortunate to get an attack of stomach cramp on the second leg and fell back to the last position. Eddie Gaze took over seventy seconds behind the team in front and over 2½ minutes from the leaders - a hopeless position; but,Eddie was not deterred and succeeded in almost catching up with Epsom & Ewell, who at this point ceased to function. Eric Penny could make no further progress although running steadily and well, and we eventually took sixth place. RESULT: (Bagley 11:11; Smithers 12:45; Gaze 11:58; Penny 11:43) The Senior race (6 x 3 miles) attracted fourteen teams. Charlie Walker took our first leg but could do no better than finish tenth with a deficit of 58secs. from Surrey A.C. Charlie Dabbs returning to racing of this type after a long series of injuries ran an exceptionally good leg to take us up to third place, only 22secs behind the leaders. Jim Heathfield could not hold this place under heavy pressure and dropped back to sixth and handed over to Clive Shippen forty seven seconds in arrears. Clive had come into the team at the last moment,although by no means fit, but managed to retain sixth place but with a margin of 72 secs from Herne Hill who were leading at this stage. Jim Masters took the fifth leg and remained in the same position, although losing ground on the teams ahead. Don Maclean who is in great form these days, went off last and with a good effort gained one place to bring us into fifth place. With a fit team we could have done better but in the circumstances the team ran well. RESULT: (Walker 15:07; Dabbs 14:16; Heathfield 15:30; Shippen 15:13; Masters 15:23; Maclean 14:44) Note; I can remember the day many years ago when all our team beat fifteen minutes - we won on that occasion - Heigho, for a return to such times!! items.s: L.A.C.RELAYS - HURLINGHAM - 19th SEPT. Report, signed C.J., of the L.A.C. Relays at Hurlingham, where Belgrave won the 4 x 440 yards in a meeting and club record 3min 20.7secs and the 4 x 110 yards, finishing sixth of eleven teams overall; with a photo of the 4 x 440 handover. Owing to the coincidence of the Poly Road Relay with this meeting, we could not field teams in the 4 x 1 mile and 4 x 880 yds steeplechase; we were also missing in the 4 x 220 yds hurdles, and the High-Jump. Our boys made amends in the remaining events however. Undoubtedly the best performance of the day was that of the victorious 4 x 440 yds team of Bernard Linley (still a junior!), Charlie Jones, Peter Eldridge and London Champion Gerry LeRoy. The main feature of this race was the really strong finishes of all lads, with Peter and Gerry both doing split times of 49.5 for their stints. Our time of 3min 20.7secs. set up a new meeting and Club record and put Birchfield, that great club of quarter-milers, into second place. We also beat Birchfield in the 4 x 110yds relay, winning in 43.2secs. With better baton-changing we would have beaten 43.0secs. The team was Peter Eldridge, Sylvan Deane, Charlie Jones and Ron Holtum,who showed a most welcome return to form in this race. An inch meant the difference between 1st and 2nd place in the Long Jump, where Dave Ansell (21'10") and Jim McGrath were squeezed out of their winner's medals. In the hammer Percy Porter and Jock Whyte gained 3rd place and John Ware, with the ever-versatile Jim McGrath,picked up 6th place in the Javelin. items.h: POLYTECHNIC H. ROAD RELAY - CHISWICK - 19th SEPT.
items.sum: Report of the Polytechnic Harriers Road Relay at Chiswick, where Belgrave's A team finished fourth with all eight men under 14 minutes, despite many absences.
items.s: POLYTECHNIC H. ROAD RELAY - CHISWICK - 19th SEPT. Report of the Polytechnic Harriers Road Relay at Chiswick, where Belgrave's A team finished fourth with all eight men under 14 minutes, despite many absences. It was regrettable that a fixture of this importance should clash with the L.A.C. Relays. Normally our middle-distance men could have split forces but on this occasion we had Newell, Robinson, Dabbs and Radford on holiday, Davies injured and Bhatia a 'flu victim; so it was decided to concentrate our remaining forces on the only major road-relay event we tackle before the "Brighton". In view of the unavailability list our less-than-usual turn-out of twenty was not unreasonable and enabled us to close an 'A' and 'B' team, and at least start a 'C'. Most of the 'A' team had done little to indicate their current form so the team was something of an unknown quantity. Len Bishop, with a season of distance running behind him, was given first leg to sharpen up his speed - as were Dennis Jones and Ken Stimpson, for the 'B' and 'C' teams. This opportunity they were duly given by Roath (Walton), who was first to the change-over, with 13:10 - fastest of the day and second fastest ever! Len ran remarkably well to finish 9th of the thirty runners, with 13:45. Charlie Walker took over five seconds down on the Valley man and in the course of chasing and catching his quarry he passed three others to give 'Jumbo' Masters the baton, in fifth spot. Our Jim got stuck into the battle with his usual spirit but had to give way to that promising Valley star, Hicks. John Moore showed that he was back on form once again, pegging back two more positions on the fourth leg to place us 4th at halfway, only 68secs behind the leaders. Alan Black held our position in the next circuit to exactly the same distance behind the third team (T.V.H.) as before - 28secs, although Woodford Green were moving up on our heels. Newly married Eric Gebbett, whose current running form was unknown, ran very well in his first race for some time, but Woodford in the shape of Eric Major (13:10) swept past both ourselves and T.V.H., to take third position. Clive Shippen, now almost fit again, held fifth place without losing ground on Woodford and handed over to Don Maclean for the final leg fifty seconds down on T.V.H. and thirty-three down on Woodford Green A.C. Don set about the latter in his most devastating style and turned the deficit into a lead of 28 secs, restoring us to a well-earned fourth place. Although we did not qualify for medals we were the only team to have run all eight men under 14mins each - consistency which should serve us well in the London-Brighton Relay - and our aggregate time was sufficent to have placed us second last year and to have won in any previous year! Brian Johnston ran exceptionally well in the 'B' team. It should not be long before he is a regular first team choice. items.s: 5¾ MILE ROAD RACE - WIMBLEDON - 26th SEPT. Report, signed W.E.L., of a club 5¾-mile road race at Wimbledon won by John Moore in 29:39, with full results and the handicap won by Chris Fairfield. Nearly thirty runners faced the starter on a fine afternoon, some with the prospect of being chosen to represent the Club in the forthcoming Brighton Relay; others with an eye to a handicap award and the remainder out to enjoy their saturday run. Don Maclean soon went to the front and looked set for a record breaking run with Charlie Walker, Clive Shippen, Eric Gebbett, John Moore and Jumbo Masters forming one group, twenty yards up on Ranjit Bhatia, Len Bishop and Mike Stearman. After leaving the common Don increased his lead and the field began to string out, but Ranjit had moved up and was profitting from a steady start. Down Copse Hill and turning into Cambridge Road the position remained much the same. But, no sooner were the hills reached than the sting went from Don and John Moore took over the lead. Before the Common was regained Clive Shippen and Charlie Walker had also passed the struggling Don and it was obvious that this was not to be his day. John went on to record a fairly comfortable win with Clive showing a welcome return to form taking second place and Charlie Walker,once again, placed in a Club race. Eric Gebbett, short of training, fell away after being prominent early on but Ranjit Bhatia and Len Bishop ran well. It was good to see Mike Stearman getting going again and we hope he will once more be a regular performer in our teams. Chris Fairfield, who has improved to the extent of four minutes since joing us last year, took the handicap with Arthur Penstone second and George Piddington a very keen lad who had also improved considerably over the past few months, in third place. The times generally were disappointing,due I was told to a troublesome wind, but more likely through general lack of training and the prospects of a win in the Brighton Relay on October 10th seem remote. items.sum: Report of the Fulham Borough Trophy meeting at Hurlingham, which Belgrave won without their middle-distance runners.
items.s: FULHAM BOROUGH TROPHY - HURLINGHAM - 26th SEPT Report of the Fulham Borough Trophy meeting at Hurlingham, which Belgrave won without their middle-distance runners. This was yet another fixture to clash with a Road-Relay, or Race - this time the Club 5¾. We were therfore minus all middle-distance runners. Charlie Jones opened our quest for points recording 3rd in the 100 yrds - he later in the afternoon easily took the 220 yds hurdles, with a respectable 25.7 secs. Despite the presence of International Adrian Breacker the 220 yards was won by Peter Eldridge in a smart 22.0secs. Cruising home to a 49.8secs quarter win, Gerry LeRoy maintained his record of the last eight weeks - always passing the post first. Making a valuable contribution to our points, D.McCorquindale scored a double in the shot and discus, with 47 and 120 ft respectively. After dropping out of the 5¾ at Wimbledon, Trevor Hart dashed down to Hurlingham to win the mile, with 4:48 - running in bare feet! A second in the sprint-relay and we had won the trophy. A good show! (By some Irish thinking the Trophy winners received prizes, whilst the 'open' winners -run in conjunction - collected medals!) items.s: LONDON CLUBS - WHITE CITY - 30th SEPT Report of the London Clubs' Continental Relay at White City, where Belgrave lost the cup to Southgate after a muddle over stations. Inserted at the end of the London-Stockholm meeting, the London Clubs' Continental Relay, 440 x 330 x 220 x 110yds. Under the fierce glare of the floodlights Gerry LeRoy stepped on to the track and settled himself into his 'blocks'. With the 'Gun' and he was away very fast, in the outside lane. Level at half-way he drew away to hand over at the quarter to Peter Eldridge, a foot ahead of International Peter Higgins. Peter, taking advantage of the 'breaking-lane after first leg' rule, tucked behind Wrighton (Southgate) but found him just a little too strong at the finish. Unbeknown to him the officials had allowed stage three to break stations, but Peter was not to know and we lost many valuable yards sorting out the tangle. Charlie Jones sped after Southgate and pulled to within two yards, but last stage officials insisted on drawn stations and a further muddle ensued. When Sylvan Deane at last got away it was too late to catch Southgate. We therefore lost our hold on this Cup. For once not entirely our own fault! 1.Southgate 1:57.0 2.BELGRAVE H. 1:57.8 3.Achilles. items.sum: Walking-section notes by Jack Goswell covering the London-Brighton walk, winter plans, new members, the club's Open 7 Miles, and news of members including Stan Vickers' 20km win in Varese.
items.s: JACK GOSWELL REPORTS Walking-section notes by Jack Goswell covering the London-Brighton walk, winter plans, new members, the club's Open 7 Miles, and news of members including Stan Vickers' 20km win in Varese. The distance season finished with a first class performance by all the lads in the London-Brighton walk. And there emerged a new Club long-distance champion, in Ray Hall. He capped a grand season by finishing 3rd, followed by George Beecham fifth and Hugh McGreechan tenth. These three occupying the first three places in the Club Championships, held in conjunction. We now start on a new Winter Season and look forward to a good crowd out pack training, from the Hall. Steady work through the winter always pays dividends when the Championships come along. We should try and start the season by annexing the Southern "Garnet Cup" race once again (it's a few years since we won this) at Trowbridge. So all you 'Junior' walkers set your target on the first week in February, for this ten mile event - and then progress on to the major Championships. We welcome new members, J.Levison, Peter Tyson, John Unwin Peter Grant and John Taylor, and look forward to their steady progress. Our Junior team needs recruits so never lose the opportunity of enrolling likely lads! We hope to have a first class muster of club men for our own Open 7 Miles, on Nov 21st. Forty years old, and the oldest open seven in the Calender, make it a "must" in the walking-world. Prizes for this event have always been of the highest standard and every help is needed to enable us to meet the high cost involved. Our thanks are due to all those stalwarts who have supported us in this endeavour. Donations would be gratefully received by the Treasurer, or Walking Hon.Sec. We are pleased to learn that George Checkley is recovering from his illness, and hopes to start training again. Congratulations to Terry Clark on his recent wedding to Janet. Several Club members attended the ceremony. Terry, who is an R.A.F. Technician, is due for Australia and we offer him the best of luck and a resumption of his brilliant walking career when he returns. Bernard Eglinton has found another sister! This time in, of all places, Cyprus where he is to stay for two years. Best wishes Bernard may your family grow, we will miss you on the Road. Stan Vickers won a very good twenty kilometer walk in Varese, Italy on Sunday 27th September, when he beat his arch rival Ken Mathews by over two minutes. He certainly pulls out the stops on his trips abroad. After a four month lay off, due to leg-injury, Eric Hall is doing that steady work which is so necessary to reach peak. May a good winter season reach a climax in the Championships, with all those improving walkers making their presence felt. And doing their best to topple those at the top. All the Best, Jack. items.sum: Report, signed E.W.H., of the London to Brighton walk, where Ray Hall was third and Belgrave lost the team race and the Edward Knott Memorial Shield to Metropolitan by a point.
items.s: LONDON TO BRIGHTON WALK - 12th SEPT Report, signed E.W.H., of the London to Brighton walk, where Ray Hall was third and Belgrave lost the team race and the Edward Knott Memorial Shield to Metropolitan by a point. The Brighton this year again dissolved into two distinct races, the two Metropolitan men, Thompson and Misson were locked together until just after Crawley, but Belgrave supporters were more interested in the third place and team race. Met. have relieved us of several long distance trophies this season and although they have provided more individual winners than any other club they had yet to win the Edward Knott Memorial Shield. George Beecham was more restrained than in other years and did not attempt to lead early on but as the leaders were doing over 7½ m.p.h. it was not surprising. The lads soon settled down and forgot all about the two wee men in front who were already burning up the road - someone said that as the morning was coolish they were keen to get to the seaside before sun-up! At Croydon Hugh McGreecgan was the leading Bel. in third place and as the field passed it was obvious that this year the team event would be a close thing. Several of the lads were not as fit as we had hoped and I heard one wife remark that her husband only turned out so that she and the children could have a day out! The gaps were appearing and with the forecast of a warm day now being fulfilled there was much speculation about times. By 20 miles Ray Hall was third in the cracking time of 3:3:00 he was being whipped along by "Digger" Clark who returned from his honeymoon to attend Ray. George was bashing along with brother Eric shedding a few stone on the bike, it is a question each year of which gives up first - the bike or Eric, but somehow they both survive. As for George I believe he smells the sea air at Streatham, Mac had eased up for a while and was developing a blister but with only 34 miles to go was not worried. Harry Shields was intent on time and motion study earlier in the year but this was not evident at this stage. However, you can always rely on the "old man" giving of his best when it is most needed. Newcomer, Jack Keown was making hay before the sun shone and Bernard Eglinton, the enigma, had begun to move through to his real place. Cyril Yescombe was very short of training but was having a go for several reasons. Percy Wilson was this year representing the Wilson clan and the other Bel. was Fred Rolfe who unfortunately had to give it best at Crawley. The race dosn't really get under way until Crawley and although Met. led in the team race all the way it was a close thing as only Don Thompson had a trouble free race; and we always felt we had a chance. Ray really consolidated his third place and George was not very keen on the idea of relinquishing his Club title, so he tore along in hot pursuit and with Don was the only one to record a faster time than last year. Mac was really in a bad way but with Fred Denny attending was able to peg back the vital place here and there. Harry closed in as fourth man, 'pot-hunter' Shields the veteran award winner; Bernard made a good recovery after a bad patch on Dale Hill and he just pipped Jack Keown by two seconds, Jack walked very well for a first-timer and was heard to say that it was easier than an Open 7. Cyril and Percy walked steadily from Crawley and gained several points but Met. with first and second were just too good, and won by a point! The attendants had the worst time, this year for instance one was given a bottle of stuff he couldn't open, somewhere around Gatwick he asked "How the hell do I open this", to which the walker gave the obvious, "Jam it in a door." Next year the attendant swears he'll take a door with him. Our attendants performed excellently and are to be congratulated! Well done Met. - but, keep the shield clean it's only on loan! Congratulations to: Don, on a great performance with the weather against you; Ray, for gaining perhaps another International vest for Belgrave and also on winning the Club Champs., and finally to Harry for the first Belgrave vets award since 1934. items.label: No. 140
items.sum: Stage-by-stage report, signed W.E.L., of the London to Brighton road relay for southern clubs, won easily by Portsmouth A.C. with Belgrave sixth, with the team result.
items.s: LONDON to BRIGHTON (SOUTHERN CLUBS) -10th OCT Stage-by-stage report, signed W.E.L., of the London to Brighton road relay for southern clubs, won easily by Portsmouth A.C. with Belgrave sixth, with the team result. It seems to have been a foregone conclusion that Portsmouth A.C., with the help of Hyman and Tulloh (with or without shoes) would win this race. And so it proved, for in no uncertain manner this 'minor' club ran away from the rest of the field to come home easy winners, nearly three minutes to spare. It seemed a travesty of justice that after months of excellent weather this should be the day for the break to occur - the rain started soon after the start and continued without a let up for the full distance. We can be satisfied that we have qualified for the next National, but much work must be put in before we can hope to close the gap between us and Portsmouth, even supposing that this club can annex the April race. At least thirty seconds must be knocked off every runners time -no easy matter but by no means improbable. 1st Stage. Ranjit Bhatia (21.17). The usual dash along the embankment did not deter this runner from India, who had endeared himself to all with whom he has come into contact. Using his head in experienced manner he dogged the leaders and moved up at Cedars Road Hill, where he proved to be better fitted than most of his opponents. Briault of Brighton, romped away to a fourteen seconds lead and our lad came in third to give us a good start. 2nd Stage. Charlie Walker (26.22). No lack of experience here although everyone crosses their fingers when 'What do you think' Charlie sets off. When the Pompey runner moved away it seemed Chas. was to have one of those days , but when Haith (T.V.H.)and later White (Woodford) caught up it seemed to act as a tonic and he stayed with them to the end, where with a typical final flourish he kept us in third place, only thirty secs. down on Pompey. 3rd Stage. Pat Newell (29.49). Pat was switched from his usual leg to this stage as he had to return to work. He held his position by steady running, until half-way up the aerodrome stretch of Purley Way when Foord of Brighton, running in fine style, sailed past. Just before reaching Purley cross-roads Herring (Blackheath) caught Pat, and on the run in John Thorpe (St.Albans) also took him, so we were back to sixth and the gap between us and the leaders, still Portsmouth, was now forty-eight seconds. 4th Stage. Clive Shippen (26.24). Our new cross-county captain running in his usual reliable fashion set about his task in steady style. Unfortunately the runners ahead with the exception of St.Albans were in better form and the gap was widened. On this stage 'Dippy' Richards of Poly brought his club into the picture for the first time with the fastest run of the day. Belgrave still sixth but 75 secs behind T.V.H. now a short lead on Pompey. 5th Stage. Jim Masters (23.05). Jim must know every inch of this section of the road and we hoped that his knowledge would help us. But although maintaining his position by passing Brighton,by losing a place to Woodford he lost considerable ground on all the other runners ahead and we finished this stage over two minutes in arrears. 6th Stage. Alan Black (13.56). Alan did the fifth fastest time of the day, and set up a new Club record, but it must have been discouraging to him to find that three of those who beat his performance were ahead of him, with the result that we remained in sixth place. 7th Stage. Mal Robinson (19.10). Our three mile track champion also set up a new Club record for this stage, and gained on three of the five teams ahead, but was unable to do more than maintain our 2min 24sec deficit. Walton, with Judd as their representative had, however, passed Malcolm who in turn had moved ahead of Blackheath. In passing Gatwick Airport, how Mal must have wished for some jet propulsion!! 8th Stage. Charlie Dabbs (31.00). On the approaches to what is probably the most difficult, and longest stage, Charlie must have felt a little overwhelmed by the company in his coach - Hyman, Peter Cl[illegible]rk, Brian Fernee, Chapman, Roath, Perkins, Mike Barratt, George Brown, Maynard, Palmer and Sando just to mention a few are not designed to rouse one's confidence. Nevertheless Chas. was not upset by these "Names" and only four were able to better his magnificent run of 31mins (yet another Belgrave best). By the time Handcross was reached we still were in sixth place but had been put in touch of the three clubs immediately ahead. Portsmouth by virtue of a record breaking run by Hyman (29.14 and 26 secs off the previous best) had gone into a 2 min lead from Thames Valley. 9th Stage. John Moore(31.35) Despite the perils of dashing down Handcross Hill rapidly, John could not resist the urge, but paid for his folly by getting cramp and having to give ground on all the runners ahead. He did recover on the latter part of the leg but the damage was done. Tulloh was taking Portsmouth into an even greater lead and T.V.H. were consolidating their second place. We were now five minutes thirty seven seconds behind. 10 Stage.Len Bishop(21.16) If Len could have kept up the pace he showed over the first mile we would have wiped out Jim Peters' name from the book, and Belgrave would have moved out of sixth place. After making up some lost ground we fell further behind at the foot of Dale Hill. 11th Stage.Jim Radford (21.25) This was Jim's first taste of the Brighton road and although his time of 21mins25secs was not outstanding he can be well pleased with his initial run in bad conditions. It compared favourably with the runners ahead and a slight gain on the leaders was made for the first time during the whole race. The fastest time of the day was less than 30 secs better than Jim's, and the experience he gained will be invaluable. 12th Stage. Don Maclean (17.55) Don was given this stage as a result of his fine last-leg efforts in the Poly and Surrey Road Relays. Although the task on this occasion was far more difficult as Woodford and Walton were 95 and 82 secs ahead, respectivly; the latter setting fastest time of the day. However , Mac set off fully determined to overcome our disadvantage but had to give best and noticeably eased up in the last mile. But for this he would have set up the fastest time of the day, his 17.55 being only 6 secs slower than Walton's Avery - thus finishing in the sixth position we had held since Purley. To sum up - a moderate performance with a few bright spots in the shape of Bhatia, Black, Dabbs, Radford and Maclean. We need some new blood so before April let us see some form from such people as Miller, Thresher, Linstead, Johnston, Stearman, and a return to the team by Hallowell, Davies and Baulch (not new blood but almost indispensable). T.V.H. gave the chance to five 'first timers' and how well they responded. We have the talent but it tends to lie dormant. items.label: No. 140
items.sum: Review by Les Stokell of the club's boys' and youths' section, praising its spirit and naming promising young runners, jumpers and throwers.
items.s: BOY'S AND YOUTH'S SECTION Review by Les Stokell of the club's boys' and youths' section, praising its spirit and naming promising young runners, jumpers and throwers. It was obvious to officials chiefly concerned with these sections at the beginning of the year, that the development of the 'Belgrave spirit' amongst the newcomers was the first most important essential. A group of youngsters had to be gathered who could be depended upon to train enthusiastically, to turn out for the Club when required and in whom could be inculcated some of the traditions and 'esprit de corps' which made Belgrave such a power in the athletics world until a few years ago. I think the course is proving a correct one, and because so much importance is attached to the 'morale' side of the lads' training, the development of the physical side i.e. fitness, strength, techniques etc., is proving so much simpler. When such keeness is shown it seems almost invidious to select particular names, but I think a few must be mentioned. David Cocks appears likely to prove a very bright star in the not too distant future; if his 4:43 mile and 2:06 half mean anything. Middle distance talent is almost in abundance so with challengers like Hampshire,Jarvis, Alan Mead, Hammond, Wiseman, Brown, Yeo, Redwood and Satchell not very far behind, David cannot afford to flag in his efforts. Our field events future is beginning to look equally bright and here I must pause to congratulate the winners of the boy's and youth's all-rounders medal competitions. Pottinger won the boy's with a score of 23 pts out of a possible 24, and J.Williams won the youth's. Pottinger,incidentally, has done twenty feet in the long-jump - Not too bad for a lad just fifteen years old. Young Wade, too, is beginning to make a name for himself, particularly in the jumps, and with Paddy Fyman,shot, Tony Moritz, discus 137 feet, and Chris Page,javelin, it appears that this side of athletics is being well taken care of. Our outstanding sprinter is undoubtedly Crosbie, who runs remarkably well every time he turns out for the club. Last, but by no means least, the youngest members of the Club; boys like Berry, Pymont (a very promising hurdler) and Nelson, having reached the ripe old age of thirteen or thereabouts have apparently made up their minds to "throw away their childish things" and to get down to serious training. Fine, but don't make it too serious yet. Remember there are still footballs to be kicked, trees to be climbed and,(dare I mention it!) exams to be passed. Les Stokell. items.s: MEDAL COMPETITION. Report, signed A.D.P., on the boys' and youths' all-round medal competitions won by D. Pottinger and J. Williams. It is encouraging to see more turning out for these competitions, though not everyone competed in each event, which is the purpose of the competition. D.Pottinger won the Boy's taking maximum points in the Shot, high-jump and long-jump; just failing by 1 point,in the 100 yds, to obtain a maximum aggregate for four events. Wiseman took 2nd place, with 3rd hotly disputed between E.Hawkins and N.Berry both with 14 pts, Hawkins taking it on highest position, although N.Berry had competed in every event. Hard lines! The youth's was won by J.Williams, who beat Dereck Wade by one point. (Dereck was last years boy's winner.) A.Mead was third, another who competed in each event, with a solid performance. In the 'boy's' it is interesting to note that D.Wiseman, who competed in all events won both the 880 yds and the 100; the 880 off 15 yds in 2:14.7, from a field of eleven, and the 100 off two yards in 11.5 secs. The corresponding times in the Youth's being, 2:16.4 and 11.9 secs. We shall be hearing more of D.Wiseman in the near future, no doubt. A.D.P. D. Two teams were entered for this event, held on 3rd Oct, and two teams turned up and finished; that in itself is quite good. In a field of 27 teams the 'A' team finished 13th and the 'B' team, 17th. Fastest effort by our boys was that of J.Yeo, whose time of 7min 33secs for the 1⅜ miles, bettered that of D.Cocks by only one second. items.s: ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING - 1959 BELGRAVE HALL -18thSEPT Report, signed H.W.S., of the 1959 Annual General Meeting, at which T.C. Jones was elected President and Stan Vickers received a presentation. The attendance of the A.G.Meeting was a little below that of recent years but even so, it was pleasing to see the goodly array of faces representing the various Club interests; especially the Youth's,Junior's and new members'. This is the one occasion when democratic priveliges can be exercised to the full, in order to ensure that those members elected to office continue to steer the Club on a progressively expanding course. Generally there were no fireworks; rather the opposite. The feeling was that the major offices should remain unchanged, and it was hoped that their re-election was a vote of confidence backed by the firm intention of giving them even more support in their many duties. The high-light of the meeting was the election of T.C.Jones as President of Belgrave Harriers. He was charmingly introduced by the retiring president F.R.Webb, who spoke of the great service that Charlie has given the Club during his membership as an athlete and official of over 30 years. A presentation to Stan Vickers to mark his European Games victory, and to commemmorate his English Native Record for the 1 hour and 8 miles walks was made amid acclamations from all. Stan expressed his appreciation of the gift and gave an amusing and most interesting account of his experience in Moscow and Helsinki. H.W.S. T.C. items.sum: Hon. Secretary's notes, signed A.A.H., on members' marriages, appeals for coaches, officials and schoolboy members, Stan Vickers' presentation and the change of magazine editors.
items.s: From the Hon.Secretary. Hon. Secretary's notes, signed A.A.H., on members' marriages, appeals for coaches, officials and schoolboy members, Stan Vickers' presentation and the change of magazine editors. We should like to express our congratulations and good wishes to Eric Hall and Mavis on their recent marriage. Mavis, as befits the only daughter of hard-working Past President Tom Morrell, has been handing out the pins and numbers for us for quite a while (and taking the money!), and our good wishes go to them both. Our good wishes also go to Eric Gebbett on his marriage, and Terry Clark who has also taken a wife unto himself. We hope to welcome Jack Brown back from Cyprus in Mar/April of next year, and it will be pleasing indeed to see him in our teams once again. In my Annual Report circulated to all members I tried to give an appraisal of our present position in the world of Athletics, and to indicate those departments in which greater strength would be a decided asset. May I again appeal to experienced Club members to come forward and assist as Coaches and as Officials? If advice or instruction is required we will try and fill the need. We are particularly anxious to build up our School-boy strength (thinking in terms of 12 years to 19!) and your help in introducing such members, and of assisting them to make the most of their talents once they are members, will be much appreciated. The presentation award made to Stan Vickers at the A.G.M., was an etched action study of Stan himself worked into the back of a mirror. An engraved tablet gave details of the wonderful records he acomplished a year ago and also referred to his winning of an European Games title last year. Stan has written expressing his sincere appreciation to the Club. We express our profound thanks to the Bishop Brothers for their great services as Joint Hon Editors, positions they now relinquish; and offer our good wishes to Malcolm Robinson and Clive Shippen who have taken over. May I ask for your full support to be given to our new Joint Hon.Editors? Our Gazette calls for team-spirit at its highest. It can breathe our hopes and aspirations, chronicle our disappointments, lead us to even greater things than we have yet known - but only if we will it to be so, and work for it to be so. As in so many other spheres of activity, if we lack enthusiasm, we lack everything. A.A.H. items.sum: The cross-country captain's call to members for regular Tuesday and Saturday training and his hopes for the coming championship season.
items.s: A Word from your CROSS-COUNTRY CAPTAIN. The cross-country captain's call to members for regular Tuesday and Saturday training and his hopes for the coming championship season. Many of you will have already read my circular letter regarding the season now upon us. If so, read it once more and ask yourself whether you are supporting the training and racing programme as well as you might. It is most important that you keep Mal Robinson or myself informed of any developments likely to affect your immediate availability; many wasted entries and cards can thus be avoided. I shall always be pleased to hear from you and can be contacted at PAD 9281 (day) or SHE 0534 (evening). To recapitulate on points previously made. Tuesday evenings and Saturday afternoons are to be treated as "Club days" and I want you to appear on at least one of these occasions per week. No one in Belgrave is good enough or bad enough to necessitate solo training at these times and it will be considered sacrilegeous to the "new" Club Spirit to do so. No one is asked to race each week but everyone is expected to meet each week. To finish umpteenth in an inter-club match matters not one iota, it's where you come in the Championship event that really counts. So let us see everyone every Saturday, and if injured let us have your vocal support instead. The season's prospects are good, but depend entirely upon your support. Charlie Dabbs and Pat Newell could both get their County colours, we have a new three mile champion, and John Moore should be a real force this winter. I therefore hope to see Belgrave win the South of Thames Junior and the L.C.C. Championships, improve a further place in the Southern and finish in the first two in the Surrey County. With the return of George Flannagan to active training, the hope of a 'come-back' by Dave Baulch and the prospect of an active season from Ron Linstead our potential is indeed great. So get to it Belgravians and step up that training! items.sum: Report of Charlie Dabbs' win in the R.R.C. and Walton 25 km track race, setting club records en route and ranking fourth in the world best-ever list.
items.s: GREAT RUN BY CHARLIE DABBS. Report of Charlie Dabbs' win in the R.R.C. and Walton 25 km track race, setting club records en route and ranking fourth in the world best-ever list. "Charlie Dabbs Causes a Surprise". This was the masterpiece of understatement in Athletics Weekly with which Sam Ferris headed his report on the R.R.C. and Walton 25KM. Track race, on 17th Oct. After his fine effort in the London-Brighton Relay 7 days earlier, Our Chas. was reported to be feeling in even greater condition, and keen to undergo an even more exacting test on his newly acquired fitness. Ivor Edmonds (Bristol A.C.) was favourite for the title with J.Heywood (H.H.H.) probable runner-up. At 5 miles Dabbs and Edmonds had a clear 44 secs. lead and a mile later were timed at 31.11 (this would have placed Chas. second in the Club 6!). After 7 miles Charlie dropped his rival and was never again troubled. En Route, Tom Carter's 10 mile Club Record of 20 odd years standing went by the board, with 52.06,and 11½ miles were covered in the hour; bettering Dave Baulch's hour record by no less than 450 yards! New Club marks were almost certainly set for 7 miles and upwards. The 15 miles was covered in 78:29.4, and although Fred Norris's English Native Record was set en route to a longer distance, Charlie was only 65 secs. outside the official mark. His 25 KM. performance ranks him fourth in the World Best-ever, behind Zatopek, Popov and Norris! His 3 mile split times were 15.37; 15.34; 15.40; 15.48 and 15.50 - remarkable consistency for an athlete who had never previously raced further than 10 miles. 1.C.Dabbs (Belgrave H.) 1.18.29.4 (15) 1.21.16.6 (25 Km) 2.I.Edmonds (Bristol A.C) 1.19.03 1.21.50 3.J.Heywood (H.H.H.) 1.23.52 1.27.07 Charlie Dabbs Charlie Dabbs won R.R.C. and Walton 25 km track race; club records for 10 miles (52.06) and the hour (11½ miles) Sam Ferris Sam Ferris wrote the Athletics Weekly report Ivor Edmonds Ivor Edmonds favourite for the title J. items.s: Note that past president Edwin Gordon has had an operation at the Exeter Eye Infirmary and is recovering well. Mr Edwin Gordon, a past president and trustee of our Club, recently entered the Exeter Eye Infirmary for an operation. We last heard that his condition was very satisfactory, and he asked that his good wishes be passed on to all his colleagues.
